The owner has more than 50 years of flying experience, over 18,000 hours of flight time, and has owned multiple aircraft throughout his aviation career. He was also honored with the prestigious Wright Brothers Master Pilot Award - a distinction achieved by only 1% of pilots in recognition of decades of safe flight operations. N66TM is finished in Platinum Sterling Silver with an Athens Blue spinner and custom red, gray, and black accent striping, N66TM has a distinctive appearance on the ramp. If you're looking for a single-owner, hangared Cirrus that has been thoughtfully maintained by an exceptionally experienced aviator, this aircraft deserves your consideration.

Equipped with the sought-after GTS package, this SR22T includes FIKI, factory air conditioning, Perspective+ by Garmin avionics, EVS, Active Traffic, Flight Stream 510, Global Connect, oxygen, and a Hartzell three-blade composite propeller. With just 645 hours total time since new, a February 2026 annual inspection, and CAPS not due until May 2028, this aircraft is an excellent option for buyers seeking an early Generation 6 Cirrus. 

Contact Kristy today for additional information.

Embark transition training is included with the purchase of N66TM. Embark is provided entirely by Cirrus Aircraft and is subject to Cirrus Aircraft’s policies and terms.

1998 CESSNA CITATION EXCEL ZP-ADE | Serial Number 560XL-5016

4,377 Total Hours | 2025 Paint | Honeywell Primus 1000

HIGHLIGHTS:

- 4,377 Total Time Since New
- 3,046 Total Landings
- Honeywell Primus 1000 Integrated Flight Deck
- Dual Pratt & Whitney Canada PW545A Engines
- Paint Redone 2026
- ADS-B Out, WAAS/LPV
- Fairchild A200S CVR
- 9 Passenger, Double Club Seating
- Flushing Aft Lavatory

Offered by JET365, this Citation Excel, Serial Number 560XL-5016, presents a well-equipped mid-size cabin with 4,377 total hours and 3,046 landings since new. The Excel pairs mid-size cabin comfort with light jet operating costs and short field capability, powered by two Pratt & Whitney Canada PW545A engines. Engine 1 shows 4,329.2 hours and 2,967 landings, Engine 2 shows 4,377.2 hours and 3,046 landings. The aircraft cruises at 430 KTAS with an NBAA IFR range of 1,858 NM, a max operating altitude of 45,000 feet, and a takeoff field length of 3,560 feet at MTOW, giving access to shorter runways unavailable to larger cabin aircraft.

The flight deck features the Honeywell Primus 1000 suite with Honeywell IFCS autopilot and flight director, dual Honeywell RCZ-833 radios, Universal UNS-1ESP FMS, dual Honeywell DME-850, Honeywell ADF-850, Honeywell Mark V TAWS, TPU-67A TCAS II, and a Fairchild A200S CVR. The aircraft is ADS-B Out and WAAS/LPV equipped.

The cabin seats 9 in double club configuration, finished in taupe leather seating with burl walnut veneer, beige textured headliner, and gold plated hardware. A forward refreshment center with pull-out countertop supports longer legs, and the aircraft is fitted with a flushing aft lavatory. The Honeywell RE100 APU shows 1,361 total hours and 2,855 landings. Exterior paint is Matterhorn White with a three-tone stripe scheme and gold trim, redone in 2025.

N862K is a highly upgraded Citation Super II featuring the Sierra Industries Williams FJ44-3A engine conversion, modern Garmin glass avionics, extended-range fuel, large baggage and entry-door modifications, and a fully refurbished cabin and exterior. The aircraft is based at Sugar Land Regional Airport (KSGR), Texas.

SIERRA SUPER II PERFORMANCE

The Sierra Super II conversion replaces the original Pratt & Whitney engines with Williams FJ44-3A turbofans, delivering improved climb, cruise efficiency, useful load and operating characteristics.

Cruise speeds approaching 400 knots at FL410
Range capability exceeding 2,000 nautical miles, depending on operating conditions
Approximately 120 gallons per hour fuel burn at cruise power settings
Improved climb performance compared with the original engine configuration

Direct climb capability to the low 40s under appropriate conditions
FADEC-equipped engines
Reduced cabin noise compared with the original engine installation
Lower engine weight contributes to increased useful load

No thrust reversers, reducing associated maintenance requirements
Extended-range configuration can provide up to approximately six hours of endurance, depending on operating conditions

The cabin was completely refurbished in 2018 by AeroPlus Interiors in Arcola, Texas and remains in very good condition. Torino Caviar seating and lower side panels are complemented by custom 100% wool carpeting in Charcoal, Charcoal Artsilk and Feather Gray.

Painted by Murmur Aircraft Services in February 2018. The exterior is finished in Matterhorn White with Midnight Blue and Charcoal Gray accent striping and presents in excellent condition.

MODIFICATIONS & UPGRADE

Sierra Super II Conversion - Williams FJ44-3A engines installed by Sierra Industries under STC SA09559AC at 7,180.9 hours aircraft total time.
Branson Extended-Range Fuel System - Additional 120-gallon fuel capacity, providing approximately 866 gallons total fuel.
Branson Large Baggage Modification - Expanded baggage capacity for increased utility on longer missions.
Sierra Large Main Entry Door - Wide-entry cabin door modification providing substantially improved passenger access.
Additional Equipment - Keith air conditioning, single-pilot wiring provisions and extensive Garmin/Jettech avionics modernization.

ENGINE PROGRAM

315.7 hours since overhaul • TAP Blue • FADEC equipped • Installed as part of the Sierra Super II conversion.
TAP Blue provides comprehensive engine maintenance coverage subject to the terms and conditions of the program.

AIRCRAFT HISTORY

N862K was originally placed on the Mexican registry and operated there from 1981 through 1996. During that period, maintenance was performed through Citation Service Centers and/or factory-authorized facilities.

In 2008, Sierra Industries completed the Williams FJ44-3A engine conversion and cabin entry-door modification.

The aircraft was located in France from 2017 through 2018. In 2017, the aircraft's wing was replaced by a Textron Citation Service Center in France following corrosion identified in the original wing. The replacement wing was sourced from Citation 551-007 and, at installation, had approximately 5,045 hours and 4,166 cycles. N862K had approximately 11,242.8 hours total time at the time of replacement.

The current owner acquired N862K in France in 2018 following a pre-purchase inspection performed at a Citation Service Center. The aircraft was subsequently brought to the United States and extensively refurbished with new exterior paint, a completely renewed interior and significant avionics modernization.

Supporting maintenance documentation, including applicable CESCOM records and selected logbook documentation, is available for review.

Configuration, Seating & Miscellaneous
This G280 features a nine (9) passenger floorplan, forward galley, aft lavatory, and in-flight accessible baggage compartment.  The seating configuration consists of a forward 4-place club with an aft cabin left-hand 3-place divan opposite a 2-place club.  The forward cabin has a pocket door, and 115V/60Hz universal outlets are found throughout the interior.
Cabin Management & Entertainment
A Gulfstream Cabin Management System (GCMS) and Audio/Video Distribution System (AVDS) provide audio and high-definition (HD) video.  Equipment includes a galley flip-down master touchscreen, dual slot Blu-ray player with media server and USB ports, cabin HDMI ports, one cabin USB port, forward and aft bulkhead 19” LCD monitors, tail camera with cockpit center AFD display capability, and a Gulfstream CabinView Passenger Flight Information System.
Communications & Data
An ICG ICS-220A satellite communications system provides voice calling via cockpit and cabin wired handsets, and Gogo AVANCE L5 broadband supplies Wi-Fi internet.
Interior Finishes
A 2022 Gulfstream refurbishment included most interior soft goods, decorative hardware re-plating, and new airstair tread, while a 2023 Gulfstream refurbishment included new countertops and recovered cabin/aft lav headliners and main cabin window line panels.
The interior features “Bird’s Eye Maple” gloss veneer, brushed “Black Pearl Satin” decorative hardware plating, and “Raincloud” Corian countertops.  Kalogridis “Mantu” wool/silk blend carpet is installed in the main cabin, and “Infinity Strobe” gray vinyl flooring is installed in the entryway.  The cabin features “Dusted Lilac” Ultraleather headliners, “Polar” Ultraleather PSU and upper sidewall panels, and “Chelsea” leather lower sidewall panels.  The cabin seats are covered in “Jefferson” leather with diamond-quilted inserts and “Monte Carlo” welting and headrest reveals.  The divan is finished in “Calobra” blended fabric.
Galley:  Forward
The galley features a countertop with pull-out work surface, sink with faucet, ice drawer with removable divider, coffee maker, microwave, cold storage compartment, and multiple miscellaneous storage compartments.
Lavatory: Aft
The lavatory is equipped with a vacuum toilet opposite a vanity with sink and faucet.

If you only ever buy one airplane, buy this one. The DA40 NG is the modern four-place single — the airplane experienced owners hand their friends when they ask what to start with, and the one a lot of them never get around to trading. Air conditioning on its own alternator, which in Florida or Texas is the difference between flying in July and talking about flying in July. Beringer wheels and brakes, electrically operated flaps, electrically adjustable rudder pedals, LED lighting throughout, perforated leather ergonomic seats and Bose six-pin plugs front and back. A 2023 airplane with a modern panel, modern comfort and nothing to update.

Description:
Order your 2027 TBM 980 today!

Daher’s TBM 980 offers the ultimate developments in avionics and comfort for a general aviation airplane.
Wherever it flies, Daher’s TBM 980 gets there faster, with speeds of 330 kts.

The Model Year 2027 TBM 980 is equipped with HomeSafe™, an emergency autoland system that can guide the aircraft to a landing in the event of pilot incapacitation. Based on Garmin’s Autoland system – and available as a part of the G3000 Prime integrated flight deck – HomeSafe™ integrates weather, traffic and terrain information to select the optimum airport for landing, considering such conditions as fuel range, flight distance and runway length.

The TBM 980 is equipped with simplified single-lever operation, the PT6E-66XT turboprop engine enables easy startup, followed by precise, predictable control and full digital envelope protection. Its other attributes are easier engine power management and parameter analysis. This reduces pilot workload by integrating all functions while protecting the engine’s life. Integrated in the TBM 980 is the autothrottle system, which automates the engine power control and monitoring. Fully integrated with the autopilot and linked to a smart engine gauge on the Garmin G3000 Prime flight deck, this single power lever can be used from climb-out to landing approach.

Donny Gabriel with Mason Amelia brings another banger. Most DA62s keep it subtle. This one doesn’t bother. N462D is exceptional in every way and redefines what a modern piston twin should be. Load up the family for a weekend escape or move colleagues for the big meeting. Either way, this one feels a lot closer to a small jet than anything in its class.

Up front, twin Austro AE330 turbo-diesels swinging MT props do the heavy lifting. Managed by full FADEC, the result is 185 KTAS on just 16 GPH of Jet-A. Speed and efficiency, finally in the same sentence. The advantage: FADEC keeps engine management to a minimum, reducing workload. The payoff: no hot starts, no flooded starts, no shock cooling... those days are over. You just smile and fly. 

The brain behind the machine: the G1000 NXi flight deck keeps you locked in and on top of your game, with synthetic vision, active traffic, XM weather, and onboard radar all working together. The GFC 700 backs you up like a rock-solid copilot, and the armrest keypad controller skips the old Garmin knob dance so you can enter what you need and keep things moving.

Inside, it’s all about comfort and feel. The cabin is wide, open, and actually usable. Real legroom. Real elbow room. And a layout that feels bigger than it should. Materials are upscale without trying too hard. The air conditioning works…SERIOUSLY works. Built-in oxygen keeps you ready for altitude, and the quiet hum of the turbo diesels lets you fade away to your favorite mental places. 

Outside, it’s anything but understated. Anthracite Blue with layered silver and black striping gives N462D a look that carries itself and rewrites ramp presence.

For a firsthand account, call or text Donny Gabriel today!

Description:
// LOCK AND KEY NAVAJO! FRESH MIKE JONES ANNUAL JUST COMPLETED //


Legendary DNA from ’77, Reborn in ‘24

Donny Gabriel of Mason Amelia is thrilled to showcase N80LK. Fit for a connoisseur, this ain’t Grandpa’s Cadillac! It offers the very latest tech, performance, style, and safety, graced by the distinction of being a “Lock & Key” Navajo, and restored by none other than Mike Jones.  

The Process. This is a guaranteed best-of-breed Navajo that transcends all others. This airplane has undergone a complete restoration, with every component and detail meticulously examined for improvement opportunities. This isn’t just about looking good. A Lock & Key Navajo is rebuilt with purpose. Every engine and airframe mod is chosen to deliver more power, more lift, and less drag. These aren’t nice-to-haves. They’re the baseline. The process was so comprehensive that it took two full years to source the perfect airframe and complete…

The Power. The Panther conversion introduces a nice performance bump with better-than-factory blueprint Lycoming engines, delivering relentless power and reliability. But the real show starts up front. The panel is unapologetically “Garminized.” Lima Kilo is sporting every product you can think of, rocking more touchscreens than a Tesla showroom, and built to flex until nothing compares.

The Experience. For those lucky enough to ride in the cabin, the brand-new, contemporary interior sets a silky-smooth ambiance. Nothing was overlooked. Every surface, every stitch, every detail is fresh, and lacquered woodwork looks wet. Cost was never a factor. The exterior appearance is next level. Winglets and Q-Tip props round out the Panther conversion and add a bold signature to its physical stance. Paired with midnight blue and white basecoats accented by gray and gold, this machine is a standout from every angle. 

The Video. N80LK offers such a tremendous opportunity that we had to see it for ourselves. We look forward to sharing our walkaround video coming soon to our YouTube channel: Looking for Higher.

For a first-hand account, call/text Donny today!

For the buyer seeking a truly outstanding Mallard rather than simply another aircraft on the market, this example deserves serious consideration.

Description:
HAWKER ISS FURY FB.10
Completely Restored • Bristol Centaurus 18 Powered • Regularly Flown
An exceptional opportunity to acquire a completely restored Hawker ISS Fury FB.10, one of the rare land-based derivatives of the legendary Hawker Sea Fury.
The ISS (Iraqi Single Seater) Fury was a purpose-built export version of the Sea Fury produced by Hawker for the Iraqi Air Force. Unlike its carrier-based Royal Navy counterpart, the ISS Fury was configured specifically for land-based operations while retaining the remarkable performance, handling qualities, and unmistakable presence of the Sea Fury design.
This aircraft has been comprehensively restored and, importantly, retains its authentic powerplant configuration with the formidable Bristol Centaurus 18-cylinder sleeve-valve radial engine.
Maintained in flying condition and flown regularly, this Fury represents considerably more than a static restoration. It is a living example of one of the finest piston-engine fighters produced during the final generation of high-performance propeller-driven combat aircraft.
With its rare Iraqi Air Force heritage, authentic Centaurus power, and complete restoration, this Hawker ISS Fury FB.10 offers an unusual combination of historical significance, originality, performance, and presence.

Description:
Peyton Lindbloom with Mason Amelia is proud to present N233RH, the kind of SR22T that makes you stop mid‑stride - not because it looks radically different, but because you can feel it’s one of the rare ones.

This 2026 SR22T GTS Generation 7+ carries just 25 hours since new, and it shows. Everything is tight, crisp, and factory‑fresh. Baja Blue over Sterling gives it that unmistakably modern Cirrus presence, but the real story is inside - where the G7 upgrades actually matter.

The moment you hit Push Button Start, the TSIO‑550‑K wakes up without the drama of hot starts or throttle choreography. The four‑blade Hartzell composite spins up smooth and quiet, and the airplane settles into that refined rhythm that only the newest airframes have.

Step into the cockpit and the difference is immediate:
14‑inch displays. Dual touchscreen controllers. Cleaner menus. Smarter logic. Faster everything.  Perspective Touch+ makes every interaction sharper, more intuitive, and more modern. Taxi routing, SurfaceWatch, CAS‑linked checklists, synoptic pages… it’s all designed to reduce workload without changing the way Cirrus pilots fly.

And then there’s the capability that actually changes the airplane: Safe Return Autoland.  
Not a concept. Not a future promise. A fully autonomous landing system sitting inside a 25‑hour SR22T. It’s the kind of feature that makes passengers exhale and pilots rethink what “single‑engine safety” can mean.

N233RH isn’t trying to be something it’s not. It’s simply one of the cleanest, lowest‑time, most fully equipped SR22T G7+ aircraft you can buy - and it flies exactly like that. Call Peyton for a first hand account today.

This is the most unique Kodiak 100 on the market. Period. 

11 Aviation is proud to represent N572SG, a two-owner Kodiak 100, Series I with the factory installed SkyTrek special edition Summit executive interior in Ebony. Very few Kodiak 100s ever left the factory with this interior, and you cannot order it anymore. From the outside it is a fully capable backcountry machine. Open the door and it boards like a business aircraft. 

SN 100-0222 is loaded: Garmin G1000 NXi, GFC 700 autopilot, TKS FIKI known-ice certification, air conditioning, external cargo pod with net, Aero Twin gravel deflector kits on the nose and mains with nose tire scraper, 29ʺ tires, 115 cu ft 10-place oxygen, GTS 800 active traffic, WX-500 Stormscope, GDL 69A SiriusXM weather and audio, and GTX 345R ADS-B In/Out.

Factory / KodiakCare maintenance through its early life, every Service Bulletin researched and complied with. No damage history. All ADs in compliance with zero recurring ADs due, per a signed compliance report dated March 2026. Type B nose fork installed. Fresh annual completed March 2026 including two brand new windshields, new brake linings, new shimmy dampener, and new TKS filters. IFR pitot-static and transponder certifications good into 2028. 

Two private owners since new. The engine has never been overhauled and has roughly 3,000 hours remaining to its 4,000-hour TBO. You are buying runway, not a punch list. 

The Kodiak 100 has 4 different variants through 2023. Series I debuted in 2015 and was the first major Series introduction for the Kodiak 100. Series I was the first Kodiak 100 to get the GFC 700 Garmin Autopilot, a true game-changer for the aircraft. Series I also introduced many cabin refinements (too many to list here) that include items like USB charging ports, new electricals, and a massively improved and quieted heating system. 

STARLINK Power supply on the glareshield!

Description:
2022 Kodiak 100 Series III | N482G | S/N 100-0316 | Approx. 550 Hours Total Time 

N482G is one of the best equipped Kodiak 100 Series III aircraft available today. The first owner ordered a full custom paint scheme at delivery, and no other Kodiak 100 wears this color. 

Inside is the Summit+ interior in Cool Grey. The seats face forward or aft, so you can run club seating, high density seating, or anything in between. The interior and cockpit present nearly new. 

The equipment list is close to everything Daher offered on the airplane: external cargo pod, TKS FIKI ice protection, 29 inch tundra tires, single point refueling, dual zone air conditioning, 10 place oxygen with the large 115 cubic foot bottle, and a Garmin G1000 NXi suite with GDL 69A datalink weather and radio, GTS 800 traffic, WX-500 Stormscope, Flight Stream 510, ChartView and SurfaceWatch. 

Damage history, stated plainly. In June 2023, under the first owner, the aircraft was damaged during an attempted takeoff from a beach runway at 164.8 hours total time. The nose wheel fork assembly, the propeller, and the engine all were affected. The aircraft was repaired by Alaska Aircraft Sales, an FAA certificated repair station, working with Daher Kodiak and Pratt & Whitney Canada.  

Installed new during that repair: a complete engine rebuild by Covington Aircraft Engines, a Pratt & Whitney authorized facility, a new Hartzell propeller, a new engine truss mount frame, a new nose landing gear assembly, a new nose gear drag brace, new nose gear fairings, a new forward cargo pod nose bowl fairing, a new left exhaust stack, a new generator control unit, and new batteries. The starter generator, alternator, oil cooler, overspeed governor and both tachometer generators were overhauled. The airframe passed a full airplane geometry inspection, a main landing gear hard landing inspection, and a wing to fuselage attach structure inspection with no defects noted. The aircraft returned to service in October 2024 with a fresh annual. 

Since the repair the airplane has flown roughly 385 hours under its second owner with no trouble. A March 2025 borescope of the engine found nothing at any inspection point. The April 2026 annual was completed by JAARS, one of the premier Kodiak operators in the world, and the pitot static, altimeter and transponder certifications were renewed in June 2026. 

Complete digital logbooks are available for review. If you want maximum Kodiak capability without the wait or the price of a new airplane, and you can look past a repaired history that is documented down to the last part number, this is the airplane. Go to 11-aviation for the log downloads and full video walk-through!

Description:
Six-seat, turbocharged, and genuinely built to haul, N950SR is a lot of capable airplane for the money. This 1979 Cessna T210N Turbo Centurion pairs a factory-new Continental engine with a 1,427-pound useful load, onboard weather radar, and a full de-ice system — the practical, load-hauling cross-country capability the 210 is famous for, without the acquisition or operating cost of a twin.

Here’s what really sets this one apart: N950SR pairs onboard weather radar (Bendix/King RDR 2000) with a full de-ice system — boots and a hot prop. Radar plus de-ice is a genuinely uncommon combination on a 210, giving you the tools to see the weather ahead and shed ice from the airframe and prop. To be clear and accurate: this is a full de-ice system — boots and hot prop, no windshield heat — and it is not certified for flight into known icing (FIKI).

Under the cowl is a factory-new Continental TSIO-520-R — a genuine new engine, not an overhaul — with just 467 hours since new. At the December 2025 annual, roughly 150 hours ago, all six cylinders were removed and re-honed, so the top end is fresh. The three-blade Q-tip propeller is equally low-time at 467 hours since prop overhaul, and the turbocharger keeps it pulling up high for a real-world 170-knot cruise in the mid-teens.

The panel is a capable, IFR-ready suite: a Garmin GNS 530W WAAS navigator, GTX 345 with ADS-B In and Out, TAS 610 active traffic, the RDR 2000 radar, and a KFC 200 autopilot with flight director. The ADS-B mandate is handled and the airframe is sorted, which makes N950SR an ideal foundation for a buyer who wants to build a modern Garmin glass panel exactly the way they want it.

We’ll be straight about the one honest trade-off: at 6,247 hours, the airframe time is above the model average. That’s exactly why it’s priced where it is — and it’s more than balanced by the factory-new engine, the freshly re-honed cylinders, the 1,427-pound useful load, the radar-and-de-ice weather capability, and clean, complete logbooks.

Based at 9K8 (Kingman, KS).

Description:
1943 BEECHCRAFT D-17S STAGGERWING
Award-Winning Restoration • 661 Hours Since Major Rebuild • Oshkosh Provenance
An excellent opportunity to acquire a beautifully presented 1943 Beechcraft D-17S Staggerwing, one of the most distinctive and highly regarded classic aircraft of the Golden Age of aviation.
Originally restored during the 1980s, this Staggerwing subsequently underwent an extensive major rebuild between 1997 and 2000. The quality of that work was recognized at EAA AirVenture Oshkosh in 2000, where the aircraft received an award following completion of the rebuild.
Since that time, the aircraft has accumulated approximately 661 hours, providing the desirable combination of an established, proven restoration and regular operational history.
The D-17S represents the ultimate development of Beechcraft’s legendary Staggerwing series, combining its unmistakable negative-stagger biplane configuration with outstanding performance, craftsmanship, and elegance.
Today, this aircraft presents as a very nice, well-established example of an increasingly desirable American classic. With its award-winning history, relatively modest time since rebuild, and timeless Staggerwing presence, it represents an attractive opportunity for the collector or owner seeking an aircraft equally at home on the flight line or the show field.

Description:
Fresh Annual!

Mandatory Service Bulletin 043 does not apply to this airplane — both engines have already been converted to the new Austro cylinder heads (rated for 1800 hours) and the next 900-hour inspection isn’t due until 1415 TT.

If you’ve been researching the DA62, you know exactly why that matters. Clean history, factory Diamond Service Center maintained since new, annual completed July 2025. Unlike other DA62s, N77DV is ready to fly.

At 90% power at 10,000 feet, this airplane cruises at 190 knots on 19 GPH of Jet A (9.5 GPH per engine). Two FADEC single-lever Austro engines means no mixture, no prop control, and if one quits you feather it with one switch and keep flying to a runway — single-engine service ceiling is 11,000 feet. No parachute repack bill either.

Full fuel payload is 765 pounds. That means full tanks and four adults with real luggage and 86 gallons of Jet-A aboard. Three rows of seating, three-door cabin access, air conditioning, TKS de-ice, trailing link landing gear, and a Garmin G1000NXi panel with the GFC 700 three-axis autopilot, weather radar, active traffic, and SiriusXM weather. 895 hours total time, always hangared, exterior and interior both 8/10.

If you’re cross-shopping this against a four-seat single in the same price range, spend a few minutes with the numbers. The DA62 answers a lot of questions that a single engine can’t. And if you need the multi-engine rating to fly it, Texas Top Aviation does that training in about a week, at your home airport.

N77DV is available now at New Braunfels National Airport (KBAZ). Digital logbooks available upon request.

Description:
N75LD is a Fairchild PT-26A Cornell II, model M-62A-3, built by Fleet Aircraft of Fort Erie, Ontario under license from Fairchild Aircraft of Hagerstown, Maryland, and powered by the 200 horsepower Ranger six cylinder inverted inline engine. The PT-26 was the enclosed canopy version of the Fairchild primary trainer family that introduced thousands of Allied cadets to flight.

WARTIME SERVICE
Delivered under the Lend Lease program as United States Army Air Forces serial 42-71130, taken on strength by the Royal Air Force as FT715, and transferred to the Royal Canadian Air Force as serial 14554. Served as a primary trainer under the British Commonwealth Air Training Plan at fields across Canada.

RESTORATION AND AWARDS
Following postwar civil registration as N75LD, with a certificate of airworthiness issued August 30, 1962, the aircraft received a complete restoration by Joe and Mark Denest of MD Aero, West Chester, Pennsylvania, recipients of multiple EAA Silver Wrench awards for Fairchild restorations. At EAA AirVenture Oshkosh 2003 the aircraft was judged Best Primary Trainer in the Warbirds division, with the Silver Wrench restoration award presented to MD Aero.

TULLIUS OWNERSHIP
In May 2002 the aircraft was purchased by Robert "Bob" Tullius, founder of the Group 44 Inc racing team that returned Jaguar to Le Mans, member of the IMSA Hall of Fame and the Motorsports Hall of Fame of America, and a lifelong aviator. It was based at his Group 44 hangar at Sebring Regional Airport, Florida, and was the subject of a published flight evaluation by Dave Unwin for Key Publishing, which described the restoration standard as immaculate. The aircraft has remained in continuous Tullius family ownership since 2002 and is airworthy and regularly flown.

OWNERSHIP CHAIN
1943: United States Army Air Forces, serial 42-71130, allocated under Lend Lease
1943: Royal Air Force FT715, then Royal Canadian Air Force 14554
1962: United States civil registry as N75LD
1989: Frank W. Young, Lexington
1996: Grand Strand Aviation Park Inc, Myrtle Beach, South Carolina
2002 to date: Robert C. Tullius and family, continuous family ownership

Description:
In the world of personal aviation, few names carry the reverence of the Beechcraft Bonanza. It is an airframe that defined the personal travel category decades ago. It remains a benchmark for speed, handling, and elegance that others have tried to emulate but few have ever truly surpassed. With this 1984 Beechcraft B36TC Bonanza, we are not just presenting an aircraft. We are presenting a living classic that has been masterfully bridged into the modern era. Stationed at Brackett Field (KPOC), this Bonanza offers the rare opportunity to own a piece of legendary aviation heritage without sacrificing a single ounce of current day utility.

Factory B36TC airframe with the desirable long-wing configuration, upgraded with a Continental IO-550 turbonormalized conversion. A unique Bonanza setup offering strong cross-country performance and high-altitude capability.

Why N6801T?

A classic is only as good as the stewardship it has received, and N6801T stands as a testament to meticulous care. With complete, continuous logs from day one, this aircraft offers the kind of transparency that serious buyers value. It captures the golden age feel of Beechcraft craftsmanship, yet it surprises you the moment you sit in the cockpit. The 2014 interior refurbishment, featuring custom Dove and Fun Silver leather and super soundproofing, respects the aircraft vintage while providing a serene, modern cabin environment that makes long distance travel feel effortless.

Key Highlights:

Timeless Performance, Modernized: At its heart lies the renowned Tornado Alley TN Conversion, paired with a Continental TNIO-550B-RA engine. With RAM Cam upgrades and TurboGAMIjectors, this aircraft delivers the classic Bonanza climb and cruise performance, optimized with 21st century reliability.

A No-Vacuum Glass Heritage: Experience the best of both worlds. The panel has been completely transformed into an all-electric, vacuum-free flight deck. Anchored by the Garmin G500 glass cockpit and dual GTN 750 (WAAS) navigators with Flightstream 510, you get the sophisticated situational awareness of a modern cruiser within the iconic lines of a classic airframe.

Comprehensive Safety and Redundancy: This Bonanza is equipped to handle the realities of modern airspace. Featuring the Garmin GTS 800 Active Traffic System, a B&C standby alternator, propeller de-ice, and a built-in CO2 sensor, it provides the peace of mind and operational security expected of a refined personal asset.

Whether you are a traditionalist who appreciates the history of the B36TC or a pilot looking for a high-performance cruiser that does not feel like a project, N6801T delivers a flying experience that is as enduring as it is enjoyable. High-resolution media folders and complete digital logbook scans are available upon request. We welcome private viewings and logbook reviews at our facility at Brackett Field. 

Contact Lipson Aviation today to discover why this classic Bonanza deserves a place in your hangar.

Description:
Only 576 Cessna 205s were ever built, and this one has the history you want. N8170Z is a 1963 Cessna 205 Super Skywagon with approximately 3,988 hours total time on the airframe. It carries no damage history and complete logbooks since new. On top of that, a STOL kit turns this big six-place hauler into a genuine short-field airplane.

The Cessna 205 is where the whole Stationair line began. Cessna took the retractable-gear 210, bolted the gear down, and revised the door and seating arrangement. The result was a six-seat utility single that could carry a real load out of a real short field. Officially designated the Model 210-5, it ran for only two model years — 1963 and 1964 — before the Cessna 206 replaced it. Because of that short run, you rarely see one come up for sale.

Put a number on that: 1,432 pounds of useful load, and long-range tanks holding 84 gallons. Top off the fuel and you still have better than 900 pounds left for people and bags. Trade some of that fuel back and all six seats fill up easily. Load or legs, you choose on the day — and not much at this price will carry either one out of a short field.

What sets N8170Z apart is the airframe underneath it. At approximately 3,988 hours total time, it sits well below the roughly 6,750-hour average for the model. Better still, it has never been damaged, and the logbooks are complete from new. For a 1963 utility airplane that has spent six decades earning its keep, that is an unusually clean record.

Consider what is actually scarce here. Cessna built only 576 of these across two model years, and very few came through six decades of utility work with a record like this one. Approximately 3,988 hours total time. No damage history. Complete logbooks since new. A JPI EDM-700 has been recording operating data along the way, so how this airplane has been flown and cared for is documented rather than guessed at.

Now look at the market. Clean 205s are asking much more and up. N8170Z is less! You are buying the scarce part — a low-time, undamaged, fully documented airframe with the STOL kit, the wheel pants and 1,432 pounds of useful load already in place — and you keep real room in your budget to finish the airplane exactly the way you want it.

For a buyer who intends to own and fly an airplane for years rather than months, that is a strong place to start.

The expensive part of modernizing an airplane this age is already behind you. N8170Z meets the ADS-B Out mandate with a uAvionix tailBeacon. Otherwise, the panel is honest 1963 factory instrumentation backed by dual Narco nav/com radios — straightforward, functional, and an inexpensive foundation for future avionics upgrades.

In addition, the airplane carries a STOL kit, an LED wingtip and strobe lighting package, wheel pants, and inertial-reel shoulder harnesses. The six-place cabin features cloth-insert seats with leather trim, and the exterior features white with black and gold striping.

If you have been waiting for a rare, low-airframe-time, six-seat hauler that you can buy right and make your own, this is the one.

Based at Georgetown Municipal Airport (KGTU) in Georgetown, Texas, just north of Austin

This is a highly capable, exceptionally clean Baron 58TC that is ready for serious cross-country travel.

Description:
It would take just short of a novel to explain the whole story on this aircraft. We will try here, but give me a call if you want to go over any questions. 
A one-off Bravo unlike any other in existence.
If you know Mooneys well, you will know that Mooney didn’t make a Bravo in 2007.  While technically correct, this plane was actually certified airworthy and delivered in by Mooney in 2007. But that is just trivia.  Here is what you really need to know about the plane.  This plane was provided by Mooney to the guys at Garmin as an experimental aircraft in ‘03 in order to certify the G-1000 for the Mooneys. You may know, that the G-1000 was not available until 2005 models. Then, the aircraft went back to Garmin and they certified the GFC-700 Autopilot in the aircraft. You may also know that the GFC-700 was not available in a Mooney until the 2007 Models.   As far was we know, it is the only Bravo in existence with the GFC-700 autopilot (unless someone paid the $75,000 price tag to upgrade from their STEC-55X). After Garmin finished, plane then went back to Mooney where it was serviced, brought up to new standards, and was production certified airworthy for the first time at 299 hours in 2007.  Then it flew off to Firewall Forward in Colorado for engine work (Crakshaft AD plus a ton of other work including the STC for the Centrilube Camshaft!).  Then back to Mooney for a redo of the interior prior to delivery to the first owner.  The end result of all this; a one-off Bravo unlike any other in existence.

HISTORY & RESTORATION:
This aircraft was manufactured for the United States Air Force by the North American Aviation Co. and was accepted by the USAF June 10, 1952.  It was utilized by the USAF at Columbus Mississippi with the 3301st Primary Training Squadron until replaced by other types in 1955.  It was then placed in storage until late 1956 when it was offset under the provisions of the Mutual Defense Assistance Program’s Grant Aid for the Uruguayan Air Force (Fuerza Aerea Uruguaya) where it served until 1991.  Its last flight was on July 24, 1986.  This aircraft was purchased with two others in 1994 and transported to Ontario Canada.
The entire aircraft has been dissembled inspected and repaired as necessary.
All hardware, cables, pulleys, seals and bearings are new.  Fuselage and wings are re-skinned as required. All wiring is new, and each individual wire is stamped with the correct numbers as per the manufacture’s original wiring drawings. All the glass was replaced with new. Instruments overhauled or replaced as required.   All “AC” hydraulic fittings are replaced with “AN” All gear and hydraulic components overhauled.
Engine overhauled by Covington with new pistons, low time heavy web cylinders and shot-peened connecting rods. Magnetos, generator, hydraulic pump, fuel pump, prop governor, carburetor, oil cooler and aux fuel bladders overhauled.

Pre-purchase inspections are welcomed in McAllen or Pleasanton, Texas, and delivery is available.

1979 CESSNA T210N CENTURION II — No Damage History · RAM Overhaul 95 SMOH · New MT 4-Blade 95 Hrs · Fresh 6/2026 Annual · GTN 750 · GFC 500

A 1979 Cessna T210N Centurion II with a fresh RAM Aircraft engine overhaul and a new MT four-blade composite propeller — both showing 95.9 hours since installation in February 2025 — a Garmin panel that has been progressively updated through 2026, and a fresh annual inspection completed in June 2026 covering airframe, engine and propeller.

The Continental TSIO-520-R was overhauled by RAM Aircraft in Waco, Texas to new-parts limits, incorporating new Superior cylinders, a new Superior camshaft and lifters, an overhauled heavy-style crankcase, new Kelly pressurized magnetos, RAM fuel nozzles, and a complete new-hose, turbocharger, controller and wastegate package. The engine is modified under RAM STC SE3630SW-D to 310 horsepower with a 1,600-hour TBO. A new MT four-blade composite propeller with new spinner and overhauled governor was installed at the same time.

The panel is built around a Garmin GTN 750 touchscreen WAAS navigator and a Garmin GFC 500 three-axis digital autopilot with yaw damper and level mode. Primary flight instrumentation is dual Garmin G5, supplemented by a Garmin GI 275 configured as a multifunction display — the GI 275 was replaced with an overhauled unit in March 2026 along with a new GMU 11 magnetometer and a new GPS antenna. A GTX 345 provides ADS-B In and Out with weather and traffic on the GTN, and a new Garmin GMA 342 audio panel was installed in May 2026. Engine and fuel data come from a JPI EDM 830 and an Aerospace Logic digital fuel display with CiES capacitance-free senders, joined in 2026 by new Electronics International amp/voltmeter and oil pressure/temperature instrumentation installed under STC.

Work through 2026 went well beyond avionics: the landing gear hydraulic pressure switch was replaced with an overhauled unit and the gear pump contactor renewed, the Arctic Air conditioning controller was relocated to the panel, dual USB charging ports and wing mirrors were added, Saf-T-Stop seat track stops were installed under STC, and surface corrosion on the pilot and copilot floorboards was removed and primed. Pitot-static, transponder and ADS-B certification was completed in May 2026 and runs through May 2028.

Useful load is approximately 1,650 pounds against an 89-gallon usable fuel capacity, giving the aircraft the load-and-go capability the turbocharged 210 is known for. Onboard oxygen and Arctic Air conditioning are installed. The interior is light gray leather in six-place configuration.

No damage history. Annual inspection completed June 2026 at 89.3 hours since major overhaul, and pitot-static/transponder/ADS-B certification is current through May 2028. Complete logbooks are available and will be provided in full to serious buyers. Aircraft is hangared at Pompano Beach Airpark (KPMP) in South Florida. Pre-purchase inspection welcome at the buyer's facility of choice.

This isn't a hangar queen that was built to look like a bush plane. It's been flown, competed, camped out of, and upgraded based on actually using it—and it has been an incredible airplane.

I’ve included photos of the airplane along with documentation showing the work and upgrades that have been done. There's other bush planes out there for sale, but you'd be hard-pressed to find one that performs like this one.

Description:
2016 CESSNA TTX — $625,000 — Based KVGT (North Las Vegas, NV) Apex Arc Blue | 1,277 TT | Air| FIKI | Tactical Weather | Active Traffic (TAS) | TAWS-B | SiriusXM | SVT | ESP | ADS-B Out | G2000 | GFC700 | WAAS | Speed Brakes | One Owner, purchased directly from Textron, not subject to any ROFR

The world's fastest certified piston single, presented in exceptional condition and backed by a maintenance pedigree few can match. N380CS has been ALWAYS Annualed at Van Bortel Aircraft since purchased from Textron — the most respected name in Cessna TTX/Corvalis service — and always hangared at home, covered when away, right down to the Bruce's custom nose gear pant and strut covers. Based in the dry Las Vegas desert (KVGT), this airframe has never seen a humid ramp for more than a few nights.

Fully equipped for real IFR cross-country travel at FL250: Garmin G2000 with latest firmware, GFC700 autopilot, WAAS, Synthetic Vision (SVT), Electronic Stability Protection (ESP), TAWS-B, active traffic (TAS), Strikefinder tactical weather, XM Datalink weather and Music, ADS-B Out, and factory Air Conditioning. TKS Flight Into Known Icing (FIKI) is exercised monthly, not left to sit — exactly how a TKS system should be maintained. LED NAV, strobe and landing lights complete the panel-to-wingtip upgrade list.

Maintenance is always ahead of schedule with no expense spared: new tires (last 2 years), new fine-wire spark plugs (2024), new fuel pump (2024), new alternator (2025), new Artex ELT battery (2026), magnetos overhauled by QAA (2024), and a new pilot door seal (2026). Oil changes every 30-40 hours with AvLab oil analysis on every change. All ADs complied with, including the V-band replacement. Logs are complete and current in both paper and digital format — no damage history.

More extras: Reiff engine preheat system, Kelly aftermarket cabin heater (runs hot even lean of peak — a known TTX pain point, solved), sheepskin seat cover, 3M exterior leading-edge protection, Jeppesen ChartView-compatible avionics, Precise Flight 02 kit with mask & new cannulas, and the complete red gear set with Bruce's heavy-duty custom cover included.

This is a turn-key, one-owner, TTX for the pilot who wants to fly, not catch up on deferred maintenance — annualed by the factory-caliber shop that knows this airframe best, meticulously maintained, and ready to go. Serious inquiries welcome.

Description: Here for sale is one of the coolest helicopters out there. This is a 1967 Hughes 369A that has a story. A true Warbird that was in the Vietnam war and now has standard airworthiness. There was a fresh overhaul done by MD to the rotor head in 2024 and the annual was completed in February 2026.

COMPREHENSIVE AIRCRAFT HISTORY:
Delivered to U.S. Army as 66-7820.
• BOC: October 1967.
• Accepted at Sharpe Army Depot
• Assigned to Directorate for Maintenance, Sharpe Army Depot Nov 1967
• Assigned to 605th Transportation Company (Aircraft Direct Support) Dec 1967
• Assigned to B Troop, 3rd Squadron, 17th Cavalry Jan 1968-Feb 1968
• Assigned to C Troop, 3rd Squadron, 17th Cavalry Mar 1968-Apr 1968
• Assigned to Headquarters Troop, 3rd Squadron, 17th Cavalry May 1968-Jun 1968
• Combat damage 18Jun68 South Vietnam and made an emergency landing. Later recovered and repaired
• Accident Jul 20, 1968 South Vietnam.
• Assigned to 605th Transportation Company (Aircraft Direct Support) Jul 1968
• Assigned to Directorate for Maintenance, Sharpe Army Depot Aug 1968-Nov 1968
• Loaned to Hughes Aircraft, Culver City Dec 1968-Aug 1969
• Assigned to Directorate for Maintenance, Sharpe Army Depot Sep 1969
• Assigned to Headquarters & Headquarters Company, 1st Brigade, 5th Infantry Division Nov 1969-Jan 1970
• Damaged on landing at LZ Cabra Jan 20, 1970 South Vietnam.
• Assigned to 142nd Transportation Company (Aircraft Direct Support) Jan 1970
• Assigned to Directorate for Maintenance, Sharpe Army Depot Feb 1970-May 1970
• Assigned to 610th Transportation Company (Aircraft Direct Support) Jun 1970
• Assigned to D Troop, 1st Squadron, 1st Cavalry Regiment Jul 1970-Jun 1972
• Assigned to D Troop, 1st Squadron, 17th Cavalry Regiment Jul 1972-Jan 1973
• Loaned to AVSCOM [United States Army Aviation Systems Command], St Louis, MS, Feb 1973-Mar 1973
• Loaned to NASA, Langley Research Center, VA, Apr 1973-Jun 1973
• Assigned to Directorate for Maintenance, Sharpe Army Depot Jul 1973-Jan 1974
• Assigned to US Army National Guard Feb 1974.
Private Owner, October 25, 1999.
• Registered as N21772.
Penfold Motors, Holland, NY, April 19, 2002-2019.

Description:
This 2024 JMB VL3 Evolution 916iS presents an excellent opportunity to acquire a highly equipped, low-time VL3 without the lead time associated with a new factory build.  With approximately 97 hours on the Hobbs, N785KG combines the performance of the 160 HP turbocharged, FADEC-equipped Rotax 916iS with a desirable avionics, and interior styling.

The aircraft features the XL cabin configuration, providing additional room and improved accommodation for larger pilots while retaining the visibility, ergonomics, and performance for which the VL3 is known.

Avionics include dual Garmin G3X 10" touchscreen displays, dual ADAHRS, Garmin GTN 650Xi NAV/COM/GPS, GTX 45R transponder, and Garmin GMC 507 autopilot controller.  Additional safety and convenience features include Smart Glide, angle of attack, heated pitot, G3X backup battery, Galaxy ballistic recovery system, and accidental gear-retraction protection.

N785KG is finished in an upgraded Limited Edition paint scheme featuring Porsche Silver, Porsche Meteor Grey, and BMW e-Copper, giving the aircraft a distinctive and premium appearance.

This is a well-equipped, exceptionally low-time example of the latest-generation VL3 and is available without the wait associated with a factory-order aircraft.

Elite Pilot Services is an authorized JMB Aircraft dealer and is familiar with the VL3 platform. Contact us for additional information, photos, or logbook scans.

Engine 1 Notes:
This engine is a first run year of manufacturer 2006 with only first run hours and cycles since new.  This engine is the perfect candidate for the Maintenance on Reliable Engines (MORE) Program STC.  The MORE Program STC for the PT6A-60A (the stock engine on the King Air B300/350) is an enhanced maintenance methodology that extends the engine's Time Between Overhaul (TBO) from the factory 3,600 hours to an 8,000-hour limit.
The program does not alter any physical parts of the engine. Instead, it replaces standard P&WC maintenance intervals with a more rigorous, tech-driven inspection routine designed to spot microscopic wear before it leads to a failure:
Periodic Borescope Inspections: Frequent internal visual checks of the hot section.
Engine Condition Trend Monitoring (ECTM): Daily data tracking of exhaust gas temperature, ITT, fuel flow, and compressor speeds to catch performance drift.
Oil Analysis: Routine spectrometric oil analysis to screen for internal metal debris.
Vibration Analysis: Regular checks to monitor the health of the compressor and turbine bearings.

Sales procedure steps:
1. Please have your financing ready - we can't hold an airplane or take a deposit "subject to financing"
2. Please have your inspector lined up, we require buyers to inspect the airplane by a FAA licensed mechanic before purchase.
3. Come see the airplane and read the log books, your inspector is welcome to use our hangar after a sales contract has been agreed to and signed by Buyer and Seller, and a refundable deposit placed with an agreed escrow service.
4. We can send copies of specific events out of the log books, and we can scan the log books, as time permits.
5. The Sales agreement includes a Hold Harmless agreement - it is an AS-IS, where-is sale with all faults, subject to your pre-buy inspection.
6. The agreement covers common-sense items, like We are only the Broker and represent only the Seller and do not make any warranties as to anything. The Seller warrants clear title and nothing else.
7.. If you are happy with the agreement, and place your refundable $ 10,000 deposit with an agreed escrow (it's refundable based upon your acceptance of your inspection), then we test fly it with you, and go to the pre-buy inspection step.
8. Price Discussions: The Seller has put thought into the price so that the airplane is attractive and competitive to similar offerings, and presents a compelling offering to Buyers.
9. You can email an offer at any time, but generally, the posted price, for the above reasons, short of an extraordinary circumstance, is the price.  We love buyers to compare, compare, compare.
10. On the pre-buy, your inspector must return the airplane to us the way we gave it to the inspector. The seller is not obligated to fix "whatever your mechanic finds". You can walk away at any time. If there's a genuine issue that the seller agrees with, it can certainly be discussed.
11. After the inspection, if the inspection is satisfactory to you, you proceed to close and pay for the airplane. Please watch and follow the due dates for funds and documents to the escrow ( thank you)
12. Like buying a new car, proof of acceptable insurance is required prior to closing.
13. The escrow process is like buying a house- the escrow will check the title status at the FAA, collect the money, file the title transfer documents at the FAA, and pay the Seller

Description:
BEFORE YOU BUY USED, COMPARE IT TO NEW.

The current used R44 market can make a brand-new aircraft a surprisingly compelling value.

HeliSafe has worked with numerous clients who began their search looking for a used R44. After comparing asking prices, remaining component life, calendar limits, equipment and future maintenance costs against buying new, the decision often became an easy one.

Instead of paying a premium for an older aircraft, they were able to choose their own paint, interior, avionics and options and take delivery of a factory-new R44 configured specifically for them.

HELISAFE KNOWS THE R44

Our experience with the R44 goes back to the very beginning.

Members of the HeliSafe team flew the very first R44s and contributed to the development of the R44 over the years through operational experience and feedback.

Today, HeliSafe owns the oldest flying R44 in the world.

That history gives us a level of R44 experience few dealers can match.

We don’t simply process an order. We help our customers configure the aircraft around how they actually plan to use it — from avionics and equipment to paint, interior and options.

WHY HELISAFE?

HeliSafe is a Robinson Helicopter Company Diamond Dealer, Robinson’s highest dealer tier.

As of September 2026, HeliSafe has taken delivery of five new Robinson helicopters in the last 60 days.

Our customers have access to a team that understands Robinson helicopters through the entire ownership experience — sales, configuration, authorized maintenance, parts, training, delivery and long-term support.

Anybody can process the paperwork on a new Robinson.
The dealer you choose matters after the paperwork is signed.

If you are considering a used R44, call us before making your decision. Let us help you compare the real numbers between used and new.

Contact HeliSafe today to discuss your new 2026 Robinson R44 Raven II.

Contact Bill Cooper for more information.

Complete logs are available, adding another important advantage for an aircraft of this vintage. Whether you're searching for a distinctive weekend flyer, a classic to enjoy at fly-ins, or simply want the experience of owning and flying one of America's recognizable vintage taildraggers, N9039K deserves serious consideration.

Description:
THE LAST STAGGERWING
BEECHCRAFT G17S — SERIAL NUMBER B-20
The 20th and Final G-Model Staggerwing Produced • Walter Beech Company Aircraft • Oshkosh Grand Champion
A truly exceptional opportunity to acquire the last G-model Staggerwing ever produced.
Serial Number B-20 holds a unique place in Beechcraft history as the 20th and final G-model Staggerwing manufactured, marking the conclusion of one of the most celebrated aircraft designs of aviation’s Golden Age.
Following its completion, B-20 was retained by Beechcraft for a period and used as a company aircraft by Walter Beech, adding extraordinary factory provenance to an already historically significant airframe.
Between 1998 and 2002, B-20 underwent an exhaustive 100-point restoration by Blue Max Aviation in San Diego, California. The quality and authenticity of the restoration were recognized immediately upon completion.
At EAA AirVenture Oshkosh 2002, B-20 was awarded:
Vintage — World War II Era — Grand Champion
As the final example of the ultimate Staggerwing variant, with direct Walter Beech association and an Oshkosh Grand Champion restoration, B-20 represents a remarkable combination of historical importance, provenance, rarity, and restoration quality.
This is not simply another Staggerwing. It is the Last Staggerwing.

Donny Gabriel with Mason Amelia proudly presents the smartest buy in the P-Baron market: N958PB. This isn’t some hangar queen or a tired old twin limping through annuals. It’s a powerhouse. N958PB is all go and no quit. Climb to the flight levels, settle into the pressurized cabin, and choose your pace. Cruise comfortably at 185 KTAS while burning just 25 gallons per hour, or push beyond 230 knots when time matters. Either way, this P-Baron delivers the payload, speed, and range to do it with confidence.

And it doesn’t just fly right. It looks the part. The 2016 paint gives it a crisp, modern appearance, while the fully refurbished 2024 interior is nothing short of stunning. Rich materials, exceptional craftsmanship, and seats that wouldn't look out of place in a modern Gulfstream elevate the cabin well beyond what you'd expect from a piston twin.

Description:
– RAM IO-550 ON THE WAY. MUST HAVE STCs. COLD A/C – 

Donny Gabriel of Mason Amelia proudly presents N77XF, a 1977 Beechcraft V35B Bonanza that combines one of the most iconic airframes ever built with smooth, big-bore Continental IO-550 power, a thoughtfully modernized IFR panel, and an impressive collection of proven Bonanza upgrades. 180 Knots True. 15 GPH. V-Tail Swag.  

If you’re unfamiliar with Beechcraft products, let us enlighten you. They’re substantial, robustly engineered, and built to last. The “Bo” is sturdy, beautifully balanced, and unmistakably solid in a way few modern piston singles can replicate. This isn’t a vintage airplane struggling to keep up. It’s a legendary contender that happens to wear one of aviation's coolest silhouettes.

The panel is modern where it matters, featuring an Aspen PFD, dual GTN 650s, a GTX 327 transponder, GDL 88 ADS-B traffic and weather, and dual USB ports, among others. Dual yokes add flexibility up front, while a semi-portable Arctic Air system delivers 7,000 BTUs of actual cooling. And the biggest upgrade is still coming: a fresh RAM-overhauled IO-550 paired with a freshly overhauled propeller. New owner. Fresh power. No looming overhaul conversation.
This V35B carries a strong collection of proven Bonanza upgrades: flap and aileron gap seals, D’Shannon ⅜” windshield, D’Shannon pilot and copilot vents, GAMI LiquidAir™ engine baffles (soon-to-be BDS baffles), Gallagher Wingtips with Orion LEDs, and more. Lastly, this one brings the V-tail look without the V-tail anxiety, thanks to the Mike Smith stub spar modification and healthy ruddervator skins.

The cosmetics aren’t new, but they are far from tired. N77XF presents remarkably well for any aircraft consistently logging nearly 400 hours a year. The luster remains, the seats are plush, the interior vibe is modern, and the fifth seat is available when the mission calls for it.

For a firsthand account of this classic V-Tail Bonanza, call/text Donny Gabriel today!

Description: N431XH is a well-equipped 1977 Bell UH-1H presented in a clean matte gray finish. The aircraft was originally manufactured and delivered directly to the Republic of Singapore Air Force, where it remained in service until 2005 before coming to the United States. Aviano Aircraft is proud to offer C-GMNL, a 1978 King Air B100. The King Air is the airplane most companies step up to when the airlines stop going where they need to go, and the B100 is the fastest version Beechcraft built of the 100 series. The difference is the engines: a pair of Garrett turbines that climb harder and perform better out of high, hot airports than the more common King Air engines. Both have plenty of life left, and both have recently been through their mid-life inspection — 315 and 653 hours ago — so the expensive engine work is behind this airplane rather than ahead of it. The four-blade propellers are in the same shape.

The cockpit is the real story. Someone spent real money modernizing it, and the centerpiece is a Garmin GTN 750 — the big touchscreen most pilots know from far newer aircraft. It handles navigation, radios, moving maps, and terrain warnings all in one box. There's a second Garmin radio for backup, a pair of Garmin transponders that already meet the current air traffic tracking requirements, and a working autopilot and flight director that will fly an approach for you. Color weather radar shows storms ahead. In short, nothing on the required-equipment list is waiting to be bought.

The cabin seats nine in a comfortable executive setup, with a wood cabinet for refreshments, a seat right by the airstair door, and a big baggage compartment in the back — one of the reasons people choose a King Air in the first place. The paint is navy blue and white. The airplane has 19,669 hours on the airframe, is registered in Canada, and the inspection status and full logbooks are available to any serious buyer.

Bottom line: a solid, comfortable, well-equipped turboprop that will carry nine people in and out of small airports, with the big-ticket maintenance recently done — and it costs a fraction of what a small jet costs to buy, fly, and maintain.

Basic Description:  The A-37 was an updated and strengthened version of the Cessna T-37 trainer. Major changes included-
*Stronger wings.
*Three  pylons on each wing.
*Larger wingtip fuel tanks of 360 liters (95 US gal) capacity.
*A General Electric GAU-2B/A 7.62 mm (0.300 in) "Minigun" Gatling-style machine gun, with   a rate of fire of 3,000 rounds/minute and 1,500 rounds of ammunition. The weapon was fitted in   the right side of the aircraft's nose. A gunsight and gun camera were also fitted.
*Better avionics for battlefield communications, navigation, and targeting.
*Tougher landing gear for rough-field operation.
*Installation of GE J-85 engines of 2400# thrust
HISTORY:  Formerly operated by the US Air Force, the aircraft was given to Vietnamese AF. The aircraft was one of two A-37 aircraft that were illegally imported into the USA via Canada. The aircraft were seized in 1989 by US customs and given to the Wings of Eagles Museum in Elmira NY. After a holding period the Museum was given permission to sell the aircraft. The current owner purchased the aircraft from a museum, and it is now FAA registered.  Customs provided a full release on the aircraft enabling civilian ownership.

Description:
I think I can claim to be the only professional helicopter salesperson who can say they’ve flown a 47G-3B-1 for a living... and it doesn’t feel that long ago! In the late ’90s, eking out a living in the Australian outback, my friends and I cut our teeth doing tourism and charter work in Bell 47s and KH1 variants. We didn’t know any better, but these days, I doubt the youngsters would be fearless enough to fly such an analogue aircraft. As the genus of the species “helicopter,” the Bell 47 comes with no engine governor, no trim system, no SCAS, and certainly no air conditioning—and you don’t really need them, since I can’t recall ever flying one with the doors on, even in the rain. 

The Bell 47 builds the best helicopter pilots, with all your senses engaged and your brain and left hand constantly modulating the engine to keep rotor RPM in the green. Nothing, except perhaps a Brantly B2 (and who in their right mind would be seen in that?), will teach you more about flying helicopters and the intricate relationship between power available, RRPM, and airspeed than a Bell 47. You’ll learn to love the smell of AVGAS again, and later in life, a whiff of 100LL will bring back memories of trying to outrun trucks on the highway. A Bell 47 gives you more visibility than an F-16, and you can screw your neck around to inspect the stab bar and linkages while on the fly. The only negative is that your bald spot will remind you if you forget your hat in the truck. 

Flying a Bell 47 is a joy—it’s engaging, raw, and feels like REAL flying. It will make you a superb pilot, able to transition into any other aircraft with a solid understanding of what really makes helicopters work.

Phoenix Caravan
FAA STC SA01850WI and SA01919WI
ASIC is unique in its ability to develop a procedure that drives out the cost of ownership caused by inspections that the manufacturer has dictated to maintain structural integrity of the aircraft through a Non-Destructive testing procedure known as Eddy Current.  This is a process that in critical areas of the aircraft the attaching hardware is removed and sensors are placed   in the structural fittings looking for fatigue cracks.  This is a repetitive inspection and causes long periods of down time causing operators to look for alternate lift sources impacting profitability.  For most of the inspections the first interval is at 12,500 operating hours followed by the same inspection only 2,500 hours later and then repeating every 2,500 hours. The cost of the inspection and the down time interval is increased on an hourly rate by five times. This makes a cost effective aircraft into something that no one wants to operate.
The ASIC FAA STC replaces the fittings originally installed by the manufacturer, starts the calculation for the next inspection at “zero” and not a short 2500 hours later.  Dividing the cost of the inspection by 20% along with the down time disappearing for 12,500 hours bringing the operating cost back in line with a younger aircraft.  The marketing name for the procedure is “Phoenix Caravan”.
The aft fuselage inspections start at 16,500 hours and repeats every 1,000 hours. All tail fittings as well as some structure and both spars in the horizontal stabilizer and both spars in the vertical fin are replaced with new. The cost of the inspection and the down time interval is increased on an hourly rate by sixteen times.
The Phoenix Caravan procedure to replace the fittings that eliminates the inspection requires special tooling along with training that is not available in any place other than ASIC, the FAA STC procedure is not available to any other facility nor can it be performed in any other location than ASIC.

For most of the inspections the first interval is at 12,500 operating hours followed by the same inspection only 2,500 hours later and then repeating every 2,500 hours. The cost of the inspection and the down time interval is increased on an hourly rate by five times. This makes a cost effective aircraft into something that no one wants to operate.
The ASIC FAA STC replaces the fittings originally installed by the manufacturer, starts the calculation for the next inspection at “zero” and not a short 2500 hours later.  Dividing the cost of the inspection by 20% along with the down time disappearing for 12,500 hours bringing the operating cost back in line with a younger aircraft.  The marketing name for the procedure is “Phoenix Caravan”.
The aft fuselage inspections start at 16,500 hours and repeats every 1,000 hours. All tail fittings as well as some structure and both spars in the horizontal stabilizer and both spars in the vertical fin are replaced with new. The cost of the inspection and the down time interval is increased on an hourly rate by sixteen times.
The Phoenix Caravan procedure to replace the fittings that eliminates the inspection requires special tooling along with training that is not available in any place other than ASIC, the FAA STC procedure is not available to any other facility nor can it be performed in any other location than ASIC.

Supported by knowledgeable Twin Cessna specialists and respected maintenance facilities with deep experience on the type, it reflects the kind of ownership buyers should seek when evaluating a cabin-class piston twin.

The McCauley three-blade propellers were overhauled concurrently, and both engines and propellers have accumulated just 565 hours since. Oil analysis has accompanied every oil change, creating a comprehensive trend history that allows buyers to evaluate engine health over time rather than relying on a single snapshot.

Behind the engines, a thoughtfully equipped panel brings modern capability with a pair of Garmin navigators, Shadin fuel flow management, Electronics International all-digital engine monitoring, and dual Garmin transponders with ADS-B In. STC'd wheel covers add a few welcome knots of cruise speed, while the VG kit increases maximum gross weight, improves low-speed handling, and lowers VMC.

Finished in Matterhorn White with Gold, Steel Blue Metallic, and Medium Silver Metallic accent stripes, the exterior continues to present exceptionally well with excellent shine and depth. Inside, the 421C truly comes into its own. Even while cruising at flight levels, the pressurization system maintains a comfortable 10,000-foot cabin altitude, and the propellers turn at just 1,800 RPM for a remarkably quiet ride. Seating for up to eight, a refreshment center, and dual executive writing tables make long trips as comfortable as they are capable.

Description:
If looking for the perfect iconic Cessna 182Q Skylane... look no further! N97875 boasts a new paint job, wonderfully upgraded avionics panel (see full specs list below), generous useful load, and numerous other upgrades.

This 182Q Skylane II includes complete and continuous logbooks and has undergone a ton of recent TLC. In October 2020, the tail was struck by a snow plow, necessitating repairs by the highly respected Beegle Aircraft Service in Greely, Colorado. The initial repairs (completed January 2022) encompassed the vertical fin, horizontal stabilizer, and elevator, and following the repair a full assessment was conducted on the aircraft and RH wing spar corrosion was identified. The RH wing was then replaced in October 2022. Following these repairs the plane went to Crider Aircraft Painting for a fresh paint job, which was completed June 2023. A plastic wingtip cap was also replaced in 2025 due to a crack in the cap. According to the seller it now flies truer and smoother than it did before the snow plow incident thanks to all the extensive work!

Current owner is looking to step up to a Cirrus SR22 following the sale. In the mean time, it is being actively flown and has been meticulously maintained.

The Cessna 182Q is truly the "sweet spot" in the Skylane market and this excellent example can be made yours today!

Description:
1974 Cessna 182P Skylane – C-GVDD

Exceptionally well-presented 1974 Cessna 182P Skylane that has benefited from extensive upgrades and refurbishment over the past several years. C-GVDD combines the proven performance and utility of the 182 with a modernized panel, upgraded autopilot, refreshed engine components, and a virtually new interior and exterior.

With only 3,575 hours total time, this aircraft has been well cared for, always hangared, and has complete logbooks dating back to new. Originally imported from the United States in 1975, the aircraft has spent its life primarily in central British Columbia and southern Alberta. The aircraft is represented as having no known damage history and no corrosion.

Powered by the proven Continental O-470-R, the engine currently has approximately 1,975 hours SMOH. In 2023, a complete top overhaul was carried out with six new Superior Millennium SA47006S-A21P cylinders installed, with approximately 275 hours since top overhaul.

The aircraft underwent a significant modernization beginning with a new instrument panel in 2022, including dual AV-30-C electronic flight instruments and an AeroCruze 100 digital autopilot. Garmin avionics, ADS-B In/Out capability, engine monitoring, fuel flow instrumentation, and satellite connectivity provide a capable and practical panel for cross-country flying.

Cosmetically, C-GVDD presents exceptionally well. In 2024, the aircraft received premium Sherwin-Williams paint, a completely renewed interior, new windows, exterior plastics and wingtips, seat rails, seat belts, and fuel bladders. Additional mechanical upgrades have included a new exhaust, alternator, tires, brakes, magnetos, and a newly installed VG kit.

C-GWVT is a rugged 1975 Cessna U206F featuring a recently overhauled Continental IO-520-F engine, extensive firewall-forward renewal and a heavy-duty Bushwheel landing-gear configuration.

Description:
→ GARMIN AVIONICS. RAM IVs. PEDIGREE MX. ←

Donny Gabriel with Mason Amelia proudly presents N32V, a low-time 1977 Cessna 340A that combines the highly desirable RAM IV engine conversion, honest cosmetics, a modernized panel, and pedigree maintenance into a standout choice for buyers who value dispatch reliability above all else.

Few aircraft deliver the combination of performance, comfort, utility, and value quite like a 340A. Dollar for dollar, pound for pound, it remains one of the most compelling aircraft in the cabin-class twin market, and N32V is a perfect example of why. Equipped with the RAM IV engine STC, N32V benefits from increased horsepower, improved climb performance, better cruise, and a gross weight increase that translates directly into enhanced payload flexibility. Pair that with a pressurized cabin, executive-class comfort, and flight-level capability, and you've got an airplane that begins to flirt with turbine-like performance while avoiding turbine acquisition costs.

Passengers will appreciate the little things in life: an airstair entry door, cold air conditioning, generous headroom and legroom, and ample baggage space for all the extras. The interior is comfortable, clean, and inviting. Nothing overdone, just a nice place to spend time. Outside, the airplane presents equally well with good luster, classic lines, and the unmistakable look of a well-kept twin Cessna.

Passengers may appreciate the comfort, but pilots will appreciate the hardware. Featuring an Aspen PFD/MFD suite, Garmin GTN 750 and GTN 650 navigators, ADS-B In/Out, a three-axis autopilot, XM datalink weather, Garmin Active Traffic, USB charging ports, flight into known icing (FIKI), and an auxiliary fuel tank, N32V is exceptionally well-equipped for long hauls.

FILE. LOAD. GO! Call or text Donny Gabriel to learn more about N32V!

Description: Originally owned by Kenmore employee after a ditching in 1972. Restored in 2010 to what it is today. Most of the fuselage skins were removed and replaced and zinc chromated. The Cutlass RG wings are internally epoxied. Cutlass RG doors with overcenter mechanisms and handles. Landing lights are in the nose and wingtips. The flaps have the trailing edge "speed bead" to allow heavy STOL work and more sudden deployment, The aircraft was built or almost new standards about 10 years ago with many airframe upgrades. The engine is a balanced Lycon overhaul at 180 HP but dynos out at closer to 200 HP. Logs are complete and every modification is legal and documented. The gross weight was not increased but the plane handles weight very easily. It is an excellent short field performer. This aircraft recieved a bronze Lindy Award at Oshkosh for being a customized classic in 2017. This aircraft is an 80% total rebuild and is the predecessor to the Bushliner overhaul program where equivalent to new 170/180/185's are built with new everything. It was appraised at $350,000 based on cost to build and equivalent types. Past history becomes irrelevant. Recently repaired from a minor ground loop and prop strike that did not affect the gear or cowling but did damage a wing tips, horizontal stabilizer, and cabin roof. Engine was torn down and propeller was replaced.

There are Cessnas—and then there is the Cardinal.

Omaha Aircraft is pleased to offer this exceptionally low-time Cessna 177RG II Cardinal with just 2,100 hours total time, complete logbooks, and no damage history.

The Cardinal RG occupies a special place in Cessna history. Designed as a more refined, modern alternative to the traditional Cessna single, the Cardinal features a sleek strutless cantilever wing, outstanding visibility, an exceptionally comfortable cabin, and some of the best entry and exit of any four-place piston single.

Add retractable landing gear, a constant-speed propeller, and the proven 200-horsepower fuel-injected Lycoming IO-360, and the Cardinal RG becomes a remarkably capable traveling airplane—combining useful cross-country performance and efficiency with the visibility and cabin comfort pilots love about a high-wing Cessna.

But perhaps what makes the Cardinal RG most special is simply the way it feels. The clean wing and responsive controls give it flying qualities unlike the more traditional Cessna singles. It is comfortable, efficient, distinctive and undeniably good-looking—an airplane equally at home traveling across the country or sitting on the ramp at your local airport.

And finding a good one is becoming increasingly difficult.

With only 2,100 hours since new, complete logbook history, and no damage history, this aircraft offers the kind of pedigree buyers look for when searching for a Cardinal worth owning.

If you've always wanted a Cardinal RG, this is one that deserves a closer look.

Description:
// BULKHEAD KIT (NO MORE AD). 5th SEATBELT STC. VG KIT. UPGRADED PANEL. //

Some airplanes spend their lives trying to prove why they're legends. This one just keeps showing up for work!

Donny Gabriel with Mason Amelia is thrilled to bring to market this heavy-hauling, no-excuses, upgraded '78 RG. N3268C is a working-class airplane with honest time, thoughtful upgrades, and plenty of life left in the tank.

The Aspen Primary Flight Display, S-TEC 30 two-axis autopilot, Garmin GNS430W GPS, Garmin GTX 345 ADS-B In/Out transponder, and JPI Engine Monitor transform this into a legitimate cross-country traveler that feels just as comfortable 500 miles from home as it does in the local area.

Prefer a more relaxed mission? Load up four passengers, crack the windows open, and ride out! The vortex generators sharpen an already legendary Skylane, while the STC'd fifth seatbelt lets you bring four passengers along for the ride. It's everything people love about a 182, just with one more seat to fill! When it's time to cover some ground, climb up, lean it out, and settle into a 150+ KTAS cruise. Either way, you'll be reminded why the retractable Skylane has such a loyal following.

If there's one thing we can say about the venerable Cessna 182RG, it's that this airplane stands tall on its own. Safe, reliable, comfortable, and affordable to own, it's the aviation equivalent of a well-kept pickup truck: never flashy, always useful, and ready whenever you are. There's a reason insurance companies and flight schools love them. They're among the most honest airplanes ever built, and N3268C stays true to that reputation.

Call/text Donny Gabriel for more information today!

For the buyer seeking a late-model Skylane with low time, an extensive avionics package, and the added appeal of air conditioning and supplemental oxygen, N2315B deserves your attention.

For a buyer seeking a turnkey CJ4 Gen2 with immediate availability, no damage history, premium connectivity, robust program coverage, and a stronger installed option package than many competing listings, 525C-0407 deserves serious consideration.
