Description:
Jake Ruiz of Mason Amelia proudly presents N821CV, a late-model 2016 Generation 5, normally aspirated Cirrus SR22 GTS featuring several upgrades that began trickling down from the upcoming G6. N821CV is exceptionally well equipped with every available factory option while still maintaining an impressive 1,162 lbs of useful load - notable for a FIKI-equipped aircraft with built-in oxygen and air conditioning. The 2016 model year also introduced upgraded door latches and the Garmin GMA 350C audio panel, bringing some refinements of the G6 into the final year of the G5. 

Compared to a turbocharged SR22, the normally aspirated (or as some call it “naturally aspirated”, so let’s simply call it “NA”) configuration eliminates approximately 80 lbs of turbo system weight, preserving valuable useful load. Along with its composite Hartzell propeller, 1CV delivers strong climb performance at lower altitudes, cooler engine operation, historically longer cylinder life, lower fuel consumption, and reduced maintenance and operating costs compared with the turbo variant. If your typical mission does not require routinely operating above approximately 15,000 feet, the NA SR22 represents an excellent balance of performance, efficiency, and capability. And if your mission includes comfortably carrying four adults with a full tank of fuel, 1CV is exceptionally well suited for the job.

Generation 5 Capability: N821CV benefits from the G5’s 200 lb gross-weight increase along with an increased first-notch flap extension speed of 150 KIAS. The result is substantially greater useful load and operational flexibility compared with earlier SR22 generations. Upgrade the Garmin G1000 Perspective avionics to Perspective+ NXi, and you have an aircraft almost identical to a G6.

With a fresh CAPS parachute, seat inflators, line cutters, and more, this G5 GTS is positioned for years of flying with very little anticipated near-term maintenance expense.

Taken as a whole, 1CV is simply the complete package: exceptionally clean, properly maintained, impressively equipped, and without a long list of expensive maintenance items waiting for its next owner. Finding all of those attributes together in one late-model G5 is becoming increasingly difficult.

For additional information and a complete set of aircraft logbooks, please email Jake Ruiz.

Go faster, for less. Reach out to Tom Donaldson to learn more!

Description:
Jake Ruiz of Mason Amelia proudly presents N654KB, an exceptionally low-time Generation 5, normally aspirated Cirrus SR22 GTS with only 765 hours total time! N654KB is currently the lowest-time G5 NA SR22 on the market with an impressive 1,200 lbs useful load - particularly impressive for a FIKI aircraft with built-in O2. 

The Cirrus Sweet Spot: Compared to a turbocharged SR22, the normally aspirated configuration saves about 80 lbs of turbo system weight, preserving valuable useful load. It also provides a stronger climb rate at lower altitudes, cooler engine operation, longer cylinder life, lower fuel consumption, and lower maintenance and operating costs than the turbo. If your typical mission does not require routinely operating above approximately 15,000 feet, the NA SR22 is a solid choice. And if your mission is to comfortably carry four adults and a full tank of fuel, 4KB is well suited to handle it.  

Generation 5 Capability: N654KB benefits from the G5’s 200 lb gross-weight increase with an increased first-notch flap extension speed of 150 KIAS. The result is substantially more useful load and greater operational flexibility than earlier SR22 generations. Upgrade the Garmin G1000 Perspective avionics to Perspective+ NXi, and you almost have yourself a G6.

Pedigree Matters: For most of its life, N654KB has been maintained by Cirrus Authorized Service Centers, backed by a very complete and well-organized set of logbooks that tells the story of a well cared-for aircraft. 4KB also benefits from a recent annual inspection completed less than 10 flight hours ago by Houston Aviation Center, a well-known Cirrus Service Center. With a fresh CAPS parachute, seat inflators, line cutters, a freshly overhauled propeller and more, this G5 GTS is positioned for years of flying with very little anticipated near-term maintenance expense.

Condition That Speaks for Itself: The photographs tell the story better than words can. N654KB’s paint and interior are in exceptional condition, reflecting the level of care this aircraft has received throughout its life.

Taken as a whole, 4KB is simply the complete package: exceptionally low time, exceptionally clean, properly maintained, well equipped, without a long list of expensive items waiting for its next owner. Finding all of that in one G5 is becoming increasingly difficult.

For additional information and a complete set of aircraft logbooks, please email Jake Ruiz.

Description:
Mason Amelia presents N869JB, a refined and highly capable aircraft occupying the sweet spot in performance, value, and luxury. 

With a low-time, finely-tuned engine strapped to the front (with dual Tornado Alley turbos spinning knots into saved time), PLUS dual Avidyne IFD440 touchscreen NAV/COMs, Garmin GI275 digital standby instrument, DFC90 autopilot, ADS-B In/Out, CIES digital fuel gauges, TKS ice protection, installed oxygen, AND AIR CONDITIONING, N869JB has it all.

The aircraft contains all the components required to upgrade to the new Vantage system, as well as the upgraded battery for the GI275 standby instrument.

The current owner has maintained this aircraft to lofty standards and consistently upgraded to make it as capable as any other Cirrus. They purchased the aircraft knowing that an engine rebuild was in the near future. Their reasoning was simple: they wanted to fly behind an engine built by the best, not one built for a pending sale. 

The engine was re-built by PowerMasters two-hundred hours after purchase, and was installed, tuned and has been maintained by former Tornado Alley staff. It is one of the smoothest and coolest running aircraft you will ever fly.

Cosmetically, photos simply cannot capture the quality and sparkle of the Imperial Red over White exterior. Very clean, very nicely equipped, and maintained to very high standards. 

Clean, quick, cool, efficient, and comfortable. The sweet spot.

Reach out now before she’s gone.

Everything comes together nicely to create a cabin that is clean, inviting, and comfortable for both the pilot and passengers. If you're looking for a classic Cirrus with an interior that has been looked after and still shows well, this aircraft will not disappoint.

DJI Agras T50 Sprayer Spreader Drone
*Price does not include batteries or charger*
The DJI Agras T50 agricultural drone features a faster pump; speeding up the already-quick spray rate of its predecessor; the Agras T40. This new drone also has a twin-rotor system; advanced stability control; nine-minute full charge; payload capacity of up to 50 KG; and multidirectional obstacle sensing and avoidance. Able to cover large swaths of farmland at 21 hectares per hour; this unit makes quick; efficient work of a variety of crucial tasks; hovering over grain farms; orchards; or livestock operations.
Spraying: The T50 can carry 40 kg of spray and disperse fine droplets in a uniform pattern at 16L/minute. Its no-leak; atomized spray system can be upgraded with an optional four-sprinkler kit. 
Spreading: With a spreading capacity of 50 kg; the T50 can spread 1500 kg/3307 lbs. per hour in a smooth; uniform manner. Features include real-time weighing and quick disassembly and cleaning. 
Surveying: For crop scouting or monitoring livestock; the T50 maintains a strong video transmission signal up to 2 km from your remote. The angle of its high-resolution FPV gimbal camera can be adjusted in real-time. 
Features
	Spreading system - Spreader motor's torque is doubled. Spiral-channel spinning disc provides uniform spread of your material. Switching to smaller hopper gates can provide more precision at a lower flow rate. 
	Spraying system - Dual atomizing centrifugal sprinklers allow you to adjust droplet size. New solenoid valves provide leak-free spraying. 
	Binocular vision provides a 3D view of terrain; enabling the drone to follow terrain; while sensing and avoiding obstacles
	Dual radar - Active phase array radars at the front and rear of the unit
	Ultra-fast charging - full charge in 9 minutes; 1500 W AC output; 1.5-meter charging cable to reach available power sources; 1500 charging cycles covered by warranty. 
	DJI RC Plus - Quad-antenna O3 transmission provides up to 2 km range. A 7-inch high-brightness screen and 8-core processor deliver clear picture and smooth control of the drone. The pole-mounted DJI Relay module helps you maintain connectivity and safe operation in steep terrain.

Twin Austro AE330 turbo-diesels push 185 knots true on just 16 gallons per hour of sweet Jet-A. That’s serious cross-country performance with road-trip fuel burn. The real game-changer is FADEC (Full Authority Digital Engine Control), handling engine management seamlessly, eliminating guesswork, and protecting your power plants from the usual wear-and-tear drama. No mixture juggling. No hot-start stress. No exceedances. Just smart automation doing what you paid for.

THE AESTHETIC: Finished in Anthracite, the exterior looks as if it were carved from liquid graphite, moving with quiet, controlled menace. Inside, the cabin, wrapped in premium bisque, feels deliberate. Wide. Airy. Intelligently designed. High-end materials and textures, thoughtfully curated. Seven real seats, not theoretical seats. The air conditioning hits like a walk-in freezer, and the built-in oxygen lets you stretch into the flight levels like a boss. The diesel hum fades into the background while the miles stack up. Whether it’s family, partners, or clients climbing aboard, this cabin delivers a travel experience closer to that of an entry-level turbine than a piston twin. Quiet. Refined. Composed.

THE EDGE: The Garmin G1000 NXi suite puts everything at your fingertips. Synthetic vision. Active traffic. XM weather. Onboard radar. The GFC 700 autopilot flies like a disciplined copilot who never gets tired and never gets sloppy. Want more details? Certified for Flight Into Known Icing (FIKI), this DA62 doesn’t blink when conditions tighten. FIKI isn’t for show. It’s for margin, options, and the days lesser aircraft stay home. Push-button starts because this isn’t 1998. A variable elevator backstop protects pitch authority without you thinking about it. Trailing-link gear with carrier-deck DNA and the finesse to lay it on like butter. Gear extension all the way to Vne gives you immediate drag when it’s time to get down in a hurry. These aren’t gimmicks. They’re quiet advantages that nobody else offers.

You get the ultimate engineered family hauler. She gets a girl’s best friend with wings. Win, win. 

Contact us for a first-hand account of this gem.

On top it is durable, easily maintained and will keep looking great for many years to come. We have developed several features for the DA50 RG to ensure the best flight performance, such as specially designed hinged double slotted flaps for high lift and superior slow speed behavior as well as many drag reduction features. The extra benefits of operating a jet fuel powered aircraft are low emissions, low fuel consumption and global availability. The 3 blade MT hydraulic variable pitch propeller features advanced blade geometry with state of the art aerodynamic airfoils for efficient performance, smoothness and low noise. The blades are built in natural composite design which leads to an exceptional vibration damping behavior and reduced weight.

Description:
→ MOST CARBON CUBS PICK ONE LANE IN LIFE. THIS ONE DIDN'T ←

Donny Gabriel with Mason Amelia proudly presents N150CC, a rare 2023 Carbon Cub factory hybrid with only 150-hrs that answers a simple question: why choose between FX-3 muscle and Super Sport handling when you can have both?

Under the cowling sits the fuel-injected Lycoming CC363i, not the CC340 you might have been expecting. The bigger surprise lies out at the wingtips, where N150CC departs from the standard FX formula with a factory-installed Carbon Cub Super Sport wing. Together, they form the foundation for one very interesting Carbon Cub, combining FX muscle with the light, playful handling that made the Super Sport so popular. Around here, we call it the FX-1.5, though with an FX-3 engine under the cowling, it might be more accurate to call it the FX-2.5. Either way, sometimes the mad scientist really does get it right.

For the STOL faithful, this FX-1.5 is equipped with extended fuel tanks holding 44 gallons, 29-inch Alaskan Bushwheels, a 3200 Baby Bushwheel tailwheel, HD brakes, Acme Black Ops suspension, and FX-3 3x3 covered landing gear. It's a no-nonsense setup for pilots who prefer their adventures beyond the pavement. The backcountry vibe doesn't come at the expense of technology. A Garmin G3X Touch anchors the panel, supported by Garmin’s GTX 345R ADS-B In/Out transponder, dual-axis autopilot with level button, XM weather/radio, and G5 backup display.

Last but certainly not least is the presentation and comfort. Finished in iconic Cub Yellow with classic lightning-bolt graphics, N150CC combines rugged capability with thoughtful amenities, including deluxe memory-foam leather seating for two, Rosen visors, rear-seat trim, USB charging ports, a 12-volt outlet, LED lighting with wig-wag functionality, an engine preheater, and an extended baggage access door. Delivering a 745-pound useful load and 480 pounds of full-fuel payload, N150CC is equally at home exploring remote strips or stretching its legs on a cross-country adventure.

For additional information, call or text Donny Gabriel today!

FOR WALKAROUND VIDEO AND ADDITIONAL MEDIA, VISIT MASONAMELIA . COM OR OUR YOUTUBE CHANNEL, “LOOKING FOR HIGHER.”

This elegant interior offers seating for fourteen (14) passengers across three distinct cabin zones, a well-appointed forward galley, and two lavatories.
The forward cabin has four club chairs with two foldout executive tables. The mid cabin zone features a 4-place conference group with a large communal table ideal for working or dining, opposite a credenza with ample storage on the right side. The aft cabin is separated by a cabin divider and boasts dual three-place divans to create a separate stateroom space. The club chairs, as well as the aft divans, are all berthable for in-flight sleeping comfort.
Amenities include a forward crew lavatory with an electric flushing toilet and a third crew member jump seat in the cockpit that is certified for takeoff and landing. The 36” forward galley on the right and an accompanying aux galley on the left house an oven, galley sink with hot & cold water, ice / drink / food storage, microwave oven, closet, and entertainment cabinet. A sliding pocket door allows for additional privacy and noise reduction. The aft cabin features a full-size passenger lavatory with electric flushing toilet, sink and storage.

We invite you to become part of this vision.

HISTORY:
Typical of Lockheed, the Aircraft is fabulous, even by today’s standards, and was considerably overbuilt and extremely modern. It is all metal, incorporating internal drooping ailerons, and a high flotation landing gear for short field performance and is extremely stable during landing, takeoffs, and ground operation.
The model 12A was designed after the slightly larger Electra 10A, as a “feeder airline”, corporate Aircraft, and for wealthy private individuals. It was regularly utilized by Charles Lindberg, Howard Hughes, and Amelia Earhart.
This Aircraft, NC18097, s/n 1250 was delivered to Phillips Petroleum from the Burbank Lockheed factory in March 1938 to supplement their DC-3.  While most 12A aircraft were trimmed in red, this one utilized green trim due to the company colors.
The Aircraft had a wonderful corporate history but was requisitioned by the military during World War II. We think it went back to Phillips after the war and was privately owned in the 60s and converted to “modern” standards at that time.
When the aircraft was purchased, approximately 2008, 12,000 hours was spent in Chino CA restoring the aircraft back to its original Phillips livery with a great deal of help from the Phillips archives. Capt. Kirk McQuown of L12 Fame was the expert on these airplanes producing several grand champions. He was primarily involved with this Restoration. Engine compartment hoses were also changed during the restoration.

Description:
MOTIVATED SELLER — MAKE OFFER
1959 McDONNELL F4H-1F PHANTOM II
SERIAL NUMBER 145310
11th Pre-Production Phantom • Operation Sageburner Aircraft • Restoration to Flight Underway
An extraordinary opportunity to acquire one of the most historically significant privately held jet warbirds in existence.
F4H-1F Phantom II, Bureau Number 145310, was delivered to the United States Navy in 1959 as the 11th pre-production Phantom, placing this aircraft at the very beginning of what would become one of the most successful and recognizable military aircraft programs in history.
OPERATION SAGEBURNER
145310 participated in the U.S. Navy's legendary Operation Sageburner program associated with the Navy's 50th Anniversary of Naval Aviation in 1961.
The program culminated in a remarkable low-altitude speed record of approximately 902 mph at only 125 feet above the ground—an extraordinary demonstration of the Phantom's performance and a significant chapter in U.S. naval aviation history.
MULTI-MILLION-DOLLAR RESTORATION
The aircraft has been undergoing an extensive restoration with the objective of returning it to airworthy condition.
The current owner has invested millions of dollars bringing the project to its present stage. Work completed to date has been documented, with components and parts appropriately identified and tagged.
This is not a project starting from zero. A substantial amount of difficult and expensive restoration work has already been accomplished.
Major items presently anticipated to complete the project include:
Overhaul of both engines
Two ejection seats
Avionics completion
Final systems completion and integration
Ground testing
Flight-test program and associated return-to-flight requirements
The current estimated cost to complete the aircraft is approximately $1.0–$2.0 million, depending upon final equipment selections, overhaul requirements, certification/authorization requirements, and the scope of work necessary during completion and flight testing.
AN OPPORTUNITY WITHOUT AN EQUAL
What makes 145310 particularly compelling is not simply its history—it is the prospect of returning an extraordinarily significant early Phantom to flight.
Subject to completion of the restoration and all applicable regulatory approvals and operating limitations, this aircraft represents a potentially unique opportunity for a private individual or organization to own and operate a flight-capable F4H/F-4 Phantom.
The combination of pre-production provenance, Operation Sageburner history, substantial restoration already completed, and the potential for private flight operation places 145310 in a category of its own.
For the right buyer, the remaining investment offers the possibility of completing something extraordinary:
A privately operated, flying McDonnell Phantom with direct ties to one of the most celebrated periods in U.S. naval aviation history.

Description:
If you're looking for one of the finest examples of a high-performance, normally aspirated traveling aircraft, N927GR deserves your attention. Combining Mooney's legendary speed and efficiency with a highly desirable avionics package and exceptional equipment, this 2006 Ovation is ready to take you anywhere in comfort and confidence.

With 1,575 hours total time on both the airframe and engine, a fresh annual inspection, and an excellent equipment list, this aircraft is turnkey and ready for its next owner. The Ovation is renowned for delivering near-200-knot cruise speeds while maintaining remarkable fuel efficiency, making it one of the most capable cross-country aircraft in its class.

The cockpit is equipped with the Garmin G1000 integrated flight deck, complemented by an STEC 55X autopilot and Garmin GTX 345R ADS-B In & Out, providing modern situational awareness with ADS-B traffic and weather. A WX-500 Stormscope offers an additional layer of weather detection, while factory air conditioning, speed brakes, and a 4-place built-in oxygen system make high-altitude, long-range travel comfortable year-round.

With an impressive 935-pound useful load, this Ovation offers outstanding mission capability for business or family travel without compromising the performance Mooney owners expect.

This is a clean, well-equipped, and exceptionally capable Mooney that is ready to fly today. Whether your mission is business travel, weekend getaways, or efficient IFR cross-country flying, N927GR delivers the performance, reliability, and comfort that have made the Ovation one of general aviation's most respected aircraft.

Description:
Patrick Jamison of Mason Amelia presents N9495V, a 1970 Mooney M20C that embodies the “affordable speed” formula that has made early Mooneys so enduring. Impressive cross-country performance, exceptional fuel efficiency, and straightforward ownership costs. N9495V builds on that proven foundation with a thoughtfully modernized panel.

The panel has an Aspen EFD1000 Pro electronic flight display, Garmin GNS 480 WAAS GPS/NAV/COM with LPV approach capability and a Garmin GNS 430 GPS/NAV/COM. A Garmin GTX 33ES provides ADS-B Out, while a JPI EDM-830 gives the pilot comprehensive engine monitoring. A modern audio panel, dedicated backup instrumentation, USB power and an updated ELT complete a well-equipped and practical IFR cockpit.

Beyond the panel, N9495V reflects years of continued ownership attention and meaningful upgrades rather than simply being preserved in its original configuration. A Power Flow tuned exhaust system and LASAR cowl enclosure further complement the M20C’s already impressive combination of performance and efficiency.

For a pilot looking to enter Mooney ownership, N9495V offers an appealing balance: classic Mooney handling and efficiency, a simple and proven normally aspirated Lycoming, and avionics that provide genuine cross-country and IFR utility. It retains the character that makes an early M20C special while incorporating the equipment that makes it useful in today’s flying environment.

Contact Pat Jamison for further details!

And who doesn’t love automatic pressurization?

The numbers tell you what she can do. Walking up to N416RL on the ramp reminds you why you wanted one. The paint has deep gloss and presents exceptionally well. Inside, the cabin is beautifully appointed and reflects the care this airplane has received. Take a close look at the photographs. The condition speaks for itself.

Low time, strong maintenance pedigree, and outstanding presentation. A serious contender for the owner-pilot ready to move into turbine ownership or upgrade within it.

Description:
Tony Beauchamp of Mason Amelia is proud to present N9131Z, a 1988 Piper Malibu with something increasingly rare among earlier PA-46s: no damage history and only two previous owners.

This isn’t just another Malibu coming to market, and I’m not just another broker representing it. I’ve flown it, maintained it, and worked on it for years. I know this airplane inside and out. N9131Z has been maintained to the absolute highest standards, with the kind of personal oversight that is almost impossible to put a price on.

Power comes from a Continental TSIO-550-C overhauled by Gann Aviation, paired with a new 3-blade Hartzell composite propeller, both clocking only 345 hours. It’s a low-time combination with plenty of muscle to support three things that elevate the Malibu: PRESSURIZATION. FIKI. AIR CONDITIONING.

And really, the Malibu’s entire appeal is wrapped up right there. It gives you the comfort and capability to climb high, avoid weather, stay cool, and cover serious ground efficiently. Add 120 gallons of fuel, a 1,247-pound useful load, Parker Hannifin landing gear, and electric flaps, and you’ve got serious capability without stepping into turbine-level operating costs. 

And finally, the cosmetics. Here’s something you simply don’t see every day on a 1988 airplane: original paint that still looks remarkably close to new. Original sometimes means old and tired. On N9131Z, it means preserved. No repaint. No cosmetic reset button. What you see is the factory finish, exceptionally well cared for over nearly four decades. Inside, classic Malibu vibes. Refurbished in 2003, the interior has been meticulously cared for. The leather remains supple and attractive, the cabin is tidy and clean, and nothing feels tired or neglected. It’s an impressive presentation that reflects years of attentive ownership.

Go fast. Go far. Go comfortably. Don't burn money doing it. THIS IS THE MALIBU TO BEAT. 

Call Tony B. for a firsthand account of N9131Z today!

Description:
Buy the airplane. Add the boxes – or not!

Every Saratoga II TC on the market today asks you to compromise on one of two things — the airframe or the panel. The clean, low-time examples wear GNS-era radios. The ones with modern touchscreen navigators are either high-time, non-glass, or well north of half a million dollars. N614DM is the one airplane in the fleet that lets you buy the hard part first and write the easy part yourself.

The hard part is already done and it cannot be bought later at any price: 2,090 hours since new, 410 hours since a major overhaul by Certified Engines, an overhauled turbocharger and a #1 cylinder IRAN completed in June 2026, a fresh February 2026 annual, and a life spent hangared. Around that sits the equipment that makes a turbocharged single actually useful in the high teens — 300-horsepower TIO-540, PiperAire air conditioning, a 50 cubic foot six-place oxygen system, Reiff preheat, standby battery, and 1,036 pounds of useful load in six seats with deluxe leather, a writing desk, and a refreshment console. The panel is Avidyne FlightMax Entegra glass with EMAX engine and fuel management, TAS600 active traffic, L3 WX-500 Stormscope, CMAX charts, and an S-TEC 55X with flight director, altitude and rate preselect, and GPSS. That is a complete situational-awareness airplane, not a project.

What it does not have is a current-production navigator, and that is precisely the opportunity. The market is currently paying a $40,000 to $60,000 premium for touchscreen navigators on this airframe — which is very nearly what the upgrade costs. This is that rare avionics decision a buyer gets back. Spend your money on the boxes you want. Or if your mission doesn’t require the current era WAAS navigators then fly it as is and you really are not sacrificing any utility.

 - MASSIVE UTILITY

 - LOW-TIME ENGINE


Donny Gabriel with Mason Amelia presents N2617M, an updated, and low-time ‘79 Cherokee Six/300. It’s the family hauler! Stuff it full of golf clubs and kids and fly to the beach. Or load up coolers, tents, and guns, and head somewhere wild. Call it the Econoline of the sky, only better!

With club seating for passengers, a 1,324 lb useful load, and a modern cockpit up front, you'll settle into the left seat and unleash 300 horses on the way to your destination. With 30 cubic feet of baggage front and rear (200 pounds total), just load up and go.

The Hershey bar wing is stable and forgiving, a docile load-hauler with good short-field performance and benign stall characteristics. A stabilator provides greater pitch authority, and a full-span anti-servo tab increases control resistance. Backed by an engine with only 30 hours since major overhaul and a Hartzell three-blade propeller, this aircraft blends predictable handling with strong, reliable performance, making it as enjoyable to fly as it is capable.
The Cherokee Six flies like a dream, even when loaded up for adventure.

In the cockpit, enjoy the modern touchscreen GTN650 navigator, dual Garmin G5’s, GTX330 Transponder, USB ports, and more useful upgrades. A fan-powered ventilation system keeps you “cool enough” on those hot days!

A pilot’s aircraft to the core, N2617M is a combination of classic function, major utility, and near-endless possibilities. For more information, call or text Donny today!

The present 8-passenger configuration consists of a forward 4-place club, followed by two rows of two forward-facing single seats.  The alternate 6-passenger configuration provides for a forward 4-place club, followed by a single row of two forward-facing seats, allowing for a larger baggage area.  The two forward cabin forward-facing seats (Seats 3 & 4) feature the “Enhanced Executive Seats Upgrade”, which includes an outboard armrest, lumbar support, literature pocket, and 180 degree swivel on each seat.  The cockpit Copilot Seat may be occupied by a passenger at Pilot’s discretion.
There is a cockpit curtain, forward wardrobe, entryway lavatory, and an aft cabin convertible baggage compartment.  A forward cabin bulkhead with sliding doors provides privacy between the forward cabin and entryway/lavatory area.  The lavatory also has a hinged privacy door that separates the cockpit and lavatory.  The forward cabin features left and right storage cabinets with the righthand cabinet upper drawer dedicated to storing two carafes.
Cabin Management
The cabin features a “Welcome Screen” iPad, LED lighting, six (6) USB outlets, and four (4) 115VAC outlets.  There are two (2) USB outlets in the cockpit.
Interior Finishes
The interior features “Zebrano” satin veneer, “Silver, Pearlite” decorative hardware plating, and gray carpet.  The cabin headliner and window panels are covered in “Fusion Rice” synthetic leather, and the lower sidewalls are finished in “Marlin” leather with “Silver Dawn” leather table shrouds.  The cabin seats are covered in “Marseille” leather with “Silver Dawn” leather seat backs/shrouds and “Edelweiss” leather accent stripes.  The pullout tables feature “Edelweiss” leather inserts.  New carpet was installed in March 2022.
Lavatory: Forward
The forward lavatory is equipped with a stowable vacuum-flushing externally serviced toilet and a sink and faucet.
Baggage Compartment
An in-flight accessible baggage compartment is located in the aftmost section of the main cabin.  The baggage area can be converted between a small and large baggage area depending on what interior configuration is installed.  The baggage compartment features a large hinged upward opening cargo compartment door with pneumatic opening and electric-assist closing.

Description:
There are airplanes you can replace.

And then there are airplanes you may never have the opportunity to own again....and Omaha Aircraft may never have the honor to represent again. 

This 1952 Piper PA-18AS-125/160 Super Cub belongs firmly in the latter category.

It left the Piper factory in Lock Haven, Pennsylvania in 1952 as a PA-18A, built for agricultural use. Four years later, in 1956, an “S” was added to its designation, certifying the aircraft for seaplane use and creating something extraordinarily uncommon: the PA-18AS.

Of the thousands of PA-18s produced, only five carry the “AS” designation.

This is one of them.

Its story becomes even more remarkable from there.
The airplane has spent its entire life in Nebraska and recently emerged from a painstaking, more than three-year, nut-and-bolt restoration by Muhle Aviation Works in Columbus, Nebraska. From spinner to tail, the objective wasn't simply to restore a Super Cub. It was to do justice to an aircraft that cannot be replaced.

The original 125-horsepower configuration has been upgraded to 160 horsepower, and with its 2,000-pound gross weight increase, this PA-18AS possesses something unusual for an aircraft of this rarity: genuine working capability.

It could be placed into a collection and preserved as one of the rarest examples of the PA-18 lineage. Or it could go back to work today, supporting commercial operations much like the airplane was originally intended to do more than seven decades ago.

That duality may be what makes this airplane most compelling.

It is historically significant without being relegated to history. Exceptionally restored without becoming merely a showpiece. Rare enough for a serious collection, yet capable enough to earn its keep.

This is not simply a beautifully restored Super Cub. Its pedigree, condition, presentation, and scarcity place it in a category where meaningful comparisons become difficult.
There simply aren't enough of them.

For the collector who has seen exceptional airplanes, owned exceptional airplanes, and understands the difference between “nice” and truly irreplaceable, this PA-18AS deserves attention.

It is the kind of aircraft that becomes the centerpiece of a collection. The one people walk past everything else in the hangar to see. The one whose story begins before the engine ever starts.

Aircraft of this caliber aren't created by writing a check. Rarity cannot be ordered. History cannot be recreated. And another one cannot simply be found when you're ready.
There are five.

And this may very well be the finest of them.

Today's buyer can spend considerably more purchasing a newly manufactured premium utility taildragger. That will buy an exceptional new airplane.
It won't buy this airplane.

This PA-18AS offers something a factory order cannot: more than seven decades of history, extraordinary rarity, a better-than-new restoration, 160 horsepower, a 2,000-pound gross weight, and a designation shared by only four other PA-18s in existence.

You can order another new airplane.

You cannot order another 1952 PA-18AS.

The opportunity isn't simply to buy a Super Cub.

It's to become the next caretaker of one of the rarest and most exceptional PA-18s in existence—and decide whether its next chapter will be spent working, collecting, or perhaps a little of both.

We are the Canadian distributor for Pipistrel Aircraft.

The Virus SW 121A – Explorer is the most advanced aircraft in its category. It is one step ahead of its older brother, the Virus SW 121. It is the result of over 30 years of Pipistrel’s experience in designing energy-efficient motor-planes, which follow the glider philosophy. The extraordinarily clean aircraft shapes enable flying with minimum power and noise, as well as the lowest fuel consumption, while keeping the performance on the same level or even better. Approved for intentional spins and Night VFR, the Explorer has the best flight characteristics in its category.

Structural efficiency is the sum of knowledge acquired in making 1500 aircraft of the same family of products. Certified and used in the most diverse environments all over the world, the entire SW 121 aircraft family fulfills the expectations of the most demanding customers who use the aircraft in hot & humid or extremely cold conditions, salty atmosphere close to the sea, or at very high altitude airports.

Even with all its advanced features and superb performance, the Explorer’s extremely efficient, environment-friendly design makes it very simple to fly and operate. The results are low running and maintenance costs, making it the most affordable choice on the market, either as an advanced trainer for the training organizations or as a personal travel aircraft for adventurous individuals.

Once you are done marveling... say hello to one of the best and most decked out Vans RV-14A builds on the planet!

The current owner is a Canadian Professional Engineer. He was the primary builder of the aircraft and began the project with the goal to fly it around the world on a formal Earth Rounders trip launching from EAA AirVenture Oshkosh 2026. While he made the trip to OSH, given the current geo-political climate he has decided to put the round-the-world plans on hold and part ways with the plane. The total cost of this build was over $375K USD, without any labor costs considered.

Following initial completion of the project in May 2025, the seller attempted a post-construction maiden flight. From a height of 10-20 feet AGL, the seller noted that the aircraft was not making ample power and attempted to land on the remaining runway. The landing was nosewheel first followed by subsequent oscillations, a runway excursion, and damage to the aircraft. Since the May 2025 incident, it was determined that the ignition system that was shipped to him was faulty. That issue was corrected and no damaged part was repaired. Each and every damaged part was replaced with an original part from the Van's Aircraft factory. Final finishing touches were then made with the assistance of EA Structures, a renowned and quality build center in British Columbia. Initial 25 hours of flight testing was conducted and completed in April 2026 from EA Structures at Chilliwack Airport in British Columbia. Since then the owner has made several training and personal flights including the AirVenture trip. It is currently hangar kept at our facility in Phillipsburg, OH while listed for sale. Until under contract, the seller will be flying it on his regular visits with his daughter who lives and works in Dayton, thus flight hours may increase slightly while on-market.

This build is a thing of beauty and is impressive in every way. The aircraft is available not only to Canadian buyers but to buyers in the US and beyond as well. Steel Aviation will assist with the straightforward import process every step of the way. Price is in USD.

Enjoy amazing and cost-effective Experimental ownership with this incredible VANS RV-14A, without all the time consuming effort of building it yourself! Call us today!!!

We are the Canadian distributor for Pipistrel Aircraft.

Velis Electro is world’s first electric powered airplane to receive a Type Certificate (EASA.A.573 TCDS). The two-seater, intended primarily for pilot training, is a game-changing aircraft in terms of technological innovations and cost-efficiency. Velis Electro can be operated commercially and is fully approved for pilot training as well as other operations. With its quietness, Velis Electro can bring flight training much closer to urban areas without adversely affecting communities’ quality of life. Ease of operation with an intuitive powertrain and impressive ergonomics come as standard.

Clean & Quiet

The Velis Electro produces zero emissions during operation and with noise levels of only 60 dBa is ultra-quiet both on the inside and outside. A revolution in sustainable flight, a game changer for ease of operation is not easy. You no longer have to dream about the future of sustainable flight, it is here and the Velis Electro has set the standard for electric flight.

Innovation & Safety

The Velis Electro was designed to be simple to operate and maintain with no compromising safety. Power comes from Pipistrelʼs own type-certified electric engine, the E-811, producing 57.6 kW from a 345 VDC electric system and inhouse developed dual battery system. This revolutionary powertrain is entirely liquid cooled, can be charged through the on board charging port with an external charger and has demonstrated levels of safety equivalent or higher than conventionally powered aircraft.

We are the Canadian distributor for Pipistrel Aircraft.

Uncompromised Performance:

The Virus SW is an exceptional aircraft holding multiple records from round the world flights to NASA challenge winners. The Virus SW’s strengths lie in its ability to fly at altitudes of 15,000ft and takeoff and land from short runways. Fully customizable with a range of powerplants and equipment options the Virus SW is the ideal aircraft for fast cross country flying, surveillance missions and advanced operations.

With more than 1,000 in operation around the world with private owners, aviation professionals, training organisations and in special mission applications the Virus SW is truly Pipistrel’s most versatile aircraft.

Fully Customizable:

Available with multiple engine choice from the 80hp Rotax 912 through to the 115hp turbocharged Rotax 914 series the Virus SW combines pure speed with unprecedented fuel economy. A host of avionics options allow for a fully customised cockpit experience including an IFR rated glass cockpit with GPS and integrated autopilot.

Aerodynamic Efficiency:

Thanks to its superior aerodynamic efficiency, state of the art composite material construction and lowest fuel consumption it its category, the Virus SW can cruise at upto 150kts and has a range of nearly 900nm. With a comfortable and quiet cabin full of high quality features such as handmade leather and a reinforced Kevlar cockpit the Virus SW really is a customer favourite.

Safety As Standard:
LSA certified and fully approved for Day/Night VFR operations with benign stall characteristics and safety built as standard.
Ballistic Parachute recovery system as standard
High turbulence penetration speed allowing high speed cruise even in turbulence • Kevlar-reinforced safety cabin and state-of-the-art composite materials to withstand the toughest of environments.
Proven track record training thousands of pilots across the world with a strong robust design.

Value:
Uncompromised performance – An airplane with no compromises and with record-breaking achievements: from several flights around-the-world to NASA challenge victories.
Flexibility in Engine Choice – Flexibility of different engines and propellers for different needs
Fully Customizable Aircraft – A fully customisable aircraft for your wishes and need

---

The Virus SW is the most economic high-speed cruiser and definitely the fastest high-wing aircraft family in its category. Multiple choice of engines defines the varants, ranging from the 80 HP to the 115 HP Turbocharged Rotax 912/914 series engines, including the fuel injected iS. Made from state-of-the-art composite materials, it is lightweight, robust and features an unprecedented useful payload of more than 300 kg (660 lbs). Virus SW offers what no competitor is able to offer and has won hearts of people world-wide. It is our best seller ever since its introduction.

NASA awarded performance

Virus SW is the only light aircraft that combines pure speed with unprecedented fuel economy. More than 1000 units were already sold world-wide, winning the hearts and acclaims of private owners, aviation professionals, training organisations and military instructors alike, just like it won the NASA challenge. Twice! Since the victories at PAV challenge 2007 and NASA GAT centennial challenge 2008, the Virus SW has been further refined and optimised for even better performance.

Virus SW is able to operate from elevations from sea-level up to 15.000 feet, take-off and land from short runways and over obstacles thanks to unique airbrakes, is the quietest light aircraft and has one of the lowest operating costs in its category.
Speed, efficiency and ultra-long range are signature for Pipistrel. Virus SW cruises faster, goes much further and flies higher than the competitors, all this while burning less fuel! Imagine flying around at over 260 km/h (140 kts), easily overflying terrain higher than 4500 m (15.000 ft) and covering distances of over 1500 km (800 NM). With Virus SW you can. All this and much more! The aircraft can be equipped by either the Rotax 912 (80 hp) 912S (100 hp), 912 iS (100 hp) and 914 Turbo (115 hp) powerplants and a large variety of avionics options.

Thanks to its superior aerodynamic efficiency, state-of-the-art composite material structure and lowest fuel consumption figures in the category, the Virus SW is ideal for High speed cross-country flying, surveillance missions, ab-initio-, advanced and extreme manoeuvre training, aerial photography and high-mountain operations. Did you know that the Virus SW has the glide ratio of 15:1 and can glide further in case of emergency than most aeroplanes?

Safety, engineering and worldwide certifications

Virus SW can be called the 300 km/h (160 kts) ultralight/microlight/LSA, but it is much more than that! With a high turbulence penetration speed (green arc) and the VNE of 302 km/h (163 kts), you can take advantage of high-speed cruise even in strong turbulence. The cockpit remains quiet and comfortable throughout the flight! The Virus SW has the largest flight safety margins in its category and can be equipped with the total ballistic parachute rescue system, offering a chance of rescue even at maximum speeds and close to the terrain.

Comfortable and luxurious cabin

The exclusive Kevlar-reinforced safety cockpit with luxurious leather interior will keep you both comfortable and safe. You can choose your own color configurations free of charge!

The instrument panel is made of carbon fibre with visible-structure and can accommodate a wide selection of modern avionics, including a full glass-cockpit IFR suite with dual-axis GPS-driven autopilot and electric or hydraulic constant-speed propeller control. The panel can be arranged according to your wishes with assistance of our skilled avionics technicians. The Virus SW has the range in excess of 1850 km (1000 nm) and you can take 40 kg (90 lbs) of luggage with you.

Upon special request, the Virus can be adapted for Special Missions, including visual/IR camera gimbals, geographical surveys, trans-oceanic-range flights and more.

ALL-NEW ROBINSON R88 | AVAILABLE TO ORDER THROUGH VOLTERRA

The Robinson R88 is an all-new, highly capable single-engine turbine helicopter designed for operators who need more passenger capacity, payload, cabin space, and mission flexibility while maintaining the straightforward operation and operating economics Robinson is known for.

Powered by the 950 shp-class Safran Arriel 2W turbine engine, the R88 is designed to accommodate two pilots plus eight passengers and offers a highly configurable 275 cu. ft. flat-floor cabin. Robinson projects an internal payload of more than 2,800 lbs, with up to approximately 1,800 lbs of payload with full fuel, more than 350 nautical miles of range, and over 3.5 hours of endurance.

Large sliding cabin doors on both sides and a unique fold-down, truck-bed-style rear door provide excellent access for passengers, equipment, bulky cargo, or a HEMS stretcher. The flexible cabin can be configured for passenger transportation, executive use, utility operations, air medical, public safety, firefighting, and other commercial missions.

The R88 features a modern Garmin avionics suite with G500H TXi displays, GTN touchscreen navigators, crew alerting, and a standard 4-axis Garmin autopilot with level mode, hover assist, limit cueing, low/high-speed protection, and low-altitude protection.

Available mission equipment is planned to include a 3,000 lb HEC-rated cargo hook, utility basket, wire-strike protection, pop-out floats, high skids, and firefighting equipment.

Every R88 will also include Safran's Serenity support package for the Arriel 2W, providing five years or 2,000 flight hours of engine support, whichever comes first.

The R88 brings true multi-mission capability to the Robinson lineup, offering the space, payload, technology, and versatility required for demanding private and commercial helicopter operations.

•	Size and Capacity: The R88 is the largest and most capable aircraft Robinson Helicopter has designed, with capacity for eight main cabin seats, two cockpit seats and a payload capacity of up to 1,800 pounds with full fuel. It has approximately 275 cubic feet of cabin volume.

•	Performance: The R88 offers a range of over 350 nautical miles and endurance exceeding 3.5 hours. The aircraft is expected to have an internal payload of more than 2,800 pounds and will be powered by a 1,000-shaft horse-power single engine in the Safran Arriel 2W.

•	Highly Configurable Interior: The highly configurable cabin features a flat floor, allowing for multiple forward and club seating configurations, effective air medical and public safety mission configurations, and multiple future seating options. A fold-down, truck-bed style rear door simplifies cargo loading and accommodates a HEMS stretcher.

•	Exterior Adaptability: The aircraft is available with standard skids or optional high skids for increased ground clearance and compatibility with a firefighting water tank. Optional equipment includes a 3,000-pound HEC-rated cargo hook, utility basket, wire strike protection kit, and pop-out floats.

•	Advanced Avionics: The R88 features a Garmin avionics suite, including large G500H TXi displays and GTN navigators with touchscreen controls. The G500H TXi includes a crew alerting system. A standard 4-axis autopilot with features such as level mode, hover assist, limit cueing, and low/high speed protection. Standard data recording with datalink and a health usage monitoring system (HUMS) simplifies operation and maintenance.

•	Enhanced Safety: The R88 incorporates dual hydraulics for pitch and roll for critical flight controls. Other standard safety features include an inlet barrier filter and impact-resistant windshields certified to Part 29 transport helicopter requirements. New LED exterior lighting, including pulse landing and taxi lights, tail rotor lighting, scene lighting, and entry lights, further enhance safety.

•	Innovative Design: The R88 introduces dual cyclic controls with removable controls on both sides, allowing the pilot in command to be in either the left or right seat with a passenger in the other seat. The aircraft will be type-certified for optional single-pilot IFR operations. The all-new interior design features comfortable, functional seating, easy-to-maintain materials, and a versatile layout.

•	Affordability: The R88 is priced starting at $3.3 million USD in current dollars for the highly equipped standard configuration.

Description:
Coming in, Wausau 5220 pull behind airport sweeper with air blowers. - MFG Brochure Attached in Service Logs

Rugged Construction Combined with Innovative Design Features
Wausau TOW SNOSaw™ High Speed Towed Runway Brooms are extremely durable providing outstanding reliability. Design features focus on ease of operation, outstanding sweeping performance, higher towing speeds, less snow build-up, and straight-forward maintenance.

High Speed Towing with Operational Safety First
With a fifth wheel or pintle eye hitch, the TOW SNOSaw can be safely operated at speeds up to 45 MPH. The trailer unit is equipped with ABS brakes. A rear steer axle for better trailing is optional. The narrow transport width of 102” allows for towing and parking capabilities that competitor’s units cannot match.

Snow Casting Stays Consistent with Less Build-Up
The unique front cap incorporates a stripper design that keeps snow casting consistent thru the life of the brush. A heated UHMW polyethylene broom hood cover is formed to a radius over the top of the assembly eliminating snow build-up on the broom head.

Powerful Drive train with a Warranty to Back It Up
The hydrostatic drive train is capable of transferring up to 600 H.P. making it compatible with the largest of available electronically controlled diesel engine power plants. All of the drive components are supplied with a manufacturer’s three year replacement warranty at no extra charge.

Dual Impeller Airblast System Provides Clean Dry Pavement
The dual impeller, dual outlet airblast system produces a high velocity air stream that blows across the swept path. One nozzle is positioned at the leading edge of the broom to further clean the pavement swept, while the other nozzle is at the trailing edge of the broom casting the snow even further as it leaves the brush

Operators Are At Ease With State-of-the-Art Control System
Broom left/right angling, up/down, airblast position, stripper cap, and quick hitch functions are accomplished with microprocessor controlled proportional hydraulics for ease of operation, trouble-shooting, and programmability allowing you to tailor the system to your individual needs.

Description:
ALSIM ALSR20 Flight Training Device

The ALSIM ALSR20 isn’t a generic training device with a Cirrus skin — it’s an exact cockpit replica of the Cirrus SR20 G6, built to put pilots in front of the same avionics, the same autopilot, and the same emergency systems they’ll fly in the real aircraft. For flight schools, Cirrus Training Centers, and ATOs looking to cut real-aircraft hours without cutting training quality, the ALSR20 is the benchmark.


KEY FEATURES:
- Genuine Cirrus Perspective+ Avionics Twin Garmin GDU 1050A displays deliver the same Primary Flight Display and Multi-Function Display pilots see in the aircraft — not a simulated approximation.
- Real GFC 700 Autopilot An authentic, AHRS-based Garmin GFC 700 digital autopilot system, giving students true-to-life automation training from day one.
- Full Garmin Suite Includes the Garmin GMA 350C all-digital audio panel and Garmin GCU 479 QWERTY keyboard interface — the same controls, the same workflow.
- CAPS® Simulation The ALSR20 replicates the Cirrus Airframe Parachute System, letting students train on this signature safety feature — accurate load, visual, and avionic behaviour included — without ever pulling the real handle.
- 210° Immersive Visual System ALSIM’s latest VFR-VS image generator delivers a wide, high-fidelity visual field for realistic approach, circuit, and low-level training.
- Dual Control Loading Electrical control loading across all three axes gives the aircraft’s true control feel, not a gaming-grade approximation.
- Instructor Operating Station Two large touchscreen displays give instructors full command of scenarios, failures, and weather — or run it remotely from any internetconnected tablet.
- Authentic Seating & Cockpit Geometry Seating position, sightlines, and ergonomics are matched to the SR20 airframe, so muscle memory transfers directly to the aircraft.


BUILT FOR CERTIFICATION:
- The ALSR20 is a Flight Training Device (FTD) Level 5, qualifying under EASA, FAA (AATD), Transport Canada, and CAAC standards — meaning hours logged in the device can count toward PPL, CPL, and Instrument Rating training, not just familiarisation.
- Backed by a two-year warranty, full installation and qualification support, and a maintenance spare-parts kit for maximum uptime.


WHY OPERATORS CHOOSE THE ALSR20:
- Reduce real-aircraft hours and operating costs without compromising training standard
- Offer CAPS emergency procedure training that’s simply not possible in the aircraft
- Attract Cirrus-affiliated students and training partnerships with a device built specifically for the type
- Log real, certifiable training hours — not just simulator familiarisation time

We are the official Pipistrel Aircraft distributor in Mexico through Wulf Aviation.

The Virus SW 121A – Explorer is one of the most advanced aircraft in the light sport and training category. It represents the evolution of the proven SW 121 platform, combining over 30 years of Pipistrel’s experience in designing highly efficient, glider-inspired aircraft.

Its exceptionally clean aerodynamic design allows for outstanding performance with very low power requirements, resulting in reduced fuel consumption, low noise levels, and highly efficient operations without compromising capability. The aircraft is approved for intentional spins and Night VFR, offering excellent and predictable flight characteristics, making it ideal for both training environments and private operations.

The Explorer is built on a platform with more than 1,500 aircraft delivered worldwide, operating in a wide range of conditions—from high-altitude airports in Mexico to hot, humid, and coastal environments. This track record ensures reliability, durability, and consistent performance even in demanding operating conditions.

Despite its advanced design and performance, the Explorer remains extremely simple to operate. Its efficiency translates directly into lower operating and maintenance costs, making it one of the most attractive options for flight schools looking to optimize training economics, as well as for private owners seeking a capable and cost-effective aircraft.

At Wulf Aviation, we work closely with Pipistrel to configure each aircraft according to the customer’s needs. All aircraft are built to order, allowing full customization in terms of equipment, configuration, and mission profile.

Description:
Core Aviation NZ - Bell Independent Representative for NZ

The Bell 505 is a versatile five-seat helicopter designed for safety, performance, and comfort. Powered by a Turbomeca Arrius 2R engine with dual-channel FADEC, it delivers exceptional fuel efficiency and reliability, while the high-inertia rotor system enhances autorotation capability. The fully integrated Garmin G1000H NXi™ flight deck with dual 10.4” displays reduces pilot workload and can be equipped with optional systems such as TIS, HTAWS, HSVT, and moving map displays for improved situational awareness. With an empty weight of 989 kg, a maximum cruise speed of 125 knots, and endurance exceeding 3.9 hours, the Bell 505 combines performance with comfort, featuring a flat cabin floor, forward-facing seats, large doors, and quiet operation meeting ICAO Stage 3 noise standards. Supported by Bell’s global, award-winning customer service network, the Bell 505 delivers advanced technology, safety, and efficiency in a compact, user-friendly platform.

Description:
Here we have this beautifully presented Boeing Stearman with a fascinating history and genuine film star status.

G-AROY was built in 1942 as a PT17 by Boeing for the United States Army Air Force. In 1959, it was transferred to the civilian Register as N56418 in Buena WA and converted to a crop sprayer. During this process, it was upgraded with the iconic PW R985 engine giving it a much needed boost in performance. In June 1961 John Jordan (Jordans Mill), a keen aviator and motor racer, imported the aircraft to the UK where it was used as a crop sprayer for several years with Aerial Farm Services Ltd. Several years later in 1965, it became John’s personal aircraft until he died in 2004.

John Jordan was an incredibly charismatic and a ‘slightly mischievous’ character, who caught the flying bug after a flight with Richard Shuttleworth at Old Warden. He joined the RAF but was dismissed for flying friends to the pub when they had been confined to barracks. Not to be stopped, he joined the ATA and ended the war having flown practically every operational aircraft in the RAF at the time. Known for his barnstorming antics, he displayed the Stearman for many years and the aircraft also featured in numerous Hollywood movies including:

1985: The Aviator, with Christopher Reeve

1986: Biggles, Adventures in time

1999: My life so far, with Colin Firth.

The aircraft has 3394 hours, with a very low time engine and propellor having only 129 hours total time. The engine, sourced from Covington (the gold standard engine shop), was fitted in 2011 after the aircraft suffered an engine failure in 2008. The opportunity was taken during this time to strip and inspect the aircraft for a full recover, install new Redline brakes and a newly overhauled engine and propellor.

The current custodian has lovingly looked after ‘ROY’ and used it primarily for charitable functions whist being flown by a professional pilot. Here is a rare opportunity for someone to acquire a much cherished and well known aircraft to be enjoyed for many years to come.

Description:
The King Air 250 is a versatile and reliable twin-turboprop aircraft from Beechcraft, a brand under Textron Aviation. It represents a perfect balance
between performance, operating efficiency, and cabin comfort, making it one of the most popular choices in the turboprop category for business and regional travel.

Powered by two Pratt & Whitney Canada PT6A-52 engines, the King Air 250 delivers strong climb performance and can cruise at speeds of up to 310 knots (approximately 357 miles per hour). Its range of around 1,720 nautical miles allows nonstop flights between key city pairs, making it ideal for regional missions. 

One of the standout features of the King Air 250 is its impressive short-field performance. Thanks to advanced technology like the Hartzell composite propellers and Raisbeck Enhanced Performance modifications, the aircraft can operate from shorter and more challenging runways, including those with gravel or grass surfaces. This allows operators to reach destinations that many jets cannot.

Inside, the King Air 250 offers a spacious, pressurized cabin that typically seats up to 9 passengers in a comfortable club-style configuration. The cabin features large oval windows that provide excellent natural light and panoramic views, while soundproofing enhancements create a quieter in
flight experience.

From a pilot’s perspective, the King Air 250 is equipped with the Collins Pro Line Fusion avionics suite, featuring touchscreen controls and advanced flight management tools. This technology enhances safety, situational awareness, and reduces pilot workload.

In summary, the King Air 250 is known for its durability, mission flexibility, low operating costs, and exceptional access to smaller airports. It remains a top choice for corporate operators, charter services, and special mission use worldwide.

Equipado com dois motores Pratt & Whitney Canada PT6A-52, o King Air 250 apresenta um excelente desempenho de subida e pode voar em cruzeiro a velocidades de até 310 nós (aproximadamente 357 milhas por hora). O seu alcance de cerca de 1720 milhas náuticas permite voos sem escalas entre pares de cidades importantes, tornando-o ideal para missões regionais. 

Uma das características mais notáveis do King Air 250 é o seu impressionante desempenho em pistas curtas. Graças a tecnologia avançada, como as hélices compostas Hartzell e as modificações Raisbeck Enhanced Performance, a aeronave pode operar a partir de pistas mais curtas e mais exigentes, incluindo aquelas com superfícies de cascalho ou relva. Isto permite aos operadores chegar a destinos que muitos jatos não conseguem alcançar.

No interior, o King Air 250 oferece uma cabina espaçosa e pressurizada que normalmente acomoda até 9 passageiros numa confortável configuração tipo clube. A cabina possui grandes janelas ovais que proporcionam excelente luz natural e vistas panorâmicas, enquanto as melhorias no isolamento acústico criam uma experiência de voo mais silenciosa.

Do ponto de vista do piloto, o King Air 250 está equipado com o conjunto de aviónica Collins Pro

• One or two stretcher systems,

Used by governments, medical operators, and humanitarian organizations worldwide, the B200 remains a benchmark in the air ambulance sector.

Description:
The Cessna 210 Centurion is a six-seat, single-engine, piston aircraft that was first flown in January 1957 and produced by Cessna. It entered the market in 1960. 

This model was designed similarly to the Cessna 182 but includes retractable landing gear, a swept tail, a new wing, and a hydraulic gear system. The fuselage was extended and made wider, while the flaps were extended to allow for a decreased landing speed.

The Cessna 210 was produced until 1986, and a total of 575 were built.

Description:
Core Aviation NZ - Bell Independent Representative for NZ

The Bell 407GXi, is a high-performance helicopter designed for efficiency, comfort, and advanced technology. Powered by a Rolls-Royce M250-C47E/4 dual-channel FADEC turbine engine, it automatically adjusts power for optimal performance and reliability. With an empty weight of 1,224 kg, a maximum cruise speed of 133 knots, and up to four hours of endurance, it can carry up to seven passengers and a full fuel load. The aircraft features the Garmin G1000H® NXi integrated flight deck with synthetic vision, wireless connectivity, terrain awareness, and customizable multi-pane displays, enhancing pilot awareness and reducing workload. Additional options include WireAware, ADS-B, radar altimeter, tail rotor camera, and Foresight MX HUMS for predictive maintenance. The Bell 407GXi combines proven global reliability—over six million flight hours—with next-generation avionics, executive interior configurations, and comprehensive global customer support, ensuring exceptional performance and value throughout ownership.

With nearly every component replaced, a clean history free of accidents, and a current March 2025 annual inspection, this hangar-kept beauty is fully airworthy and ready for its next mission.

Presented for sale is this exceptionally appealing 2016 Bristell NG5 Speedwing, G-XFTF, with just 243 total hours and two owners from new. Finished in a beautiful baby-blue colour scheme with a smart and very well-presented interior, this is an aircraft that looks every bit as good in person as it does in photographs. It has clearly been well loved and carefully looked after by its previous owners and is now ready to find a new owner to continue enjoying everything this highly capable two-seat aircraft has to offer.

‍

The Bristell NG5 is sleek and enjoyable aircraft combining a comfortable two-seat side-by-side cockpit with clean lines and sporty character on the outside. TF has a particularly purposeful appearance with excellent visibility for both local flying, touring or just simply enjoying time in the air. It is a fantastic choice for a pilot looking to move into a modern, well-equipped aircraft that offers an engaging flying experience.

‍

Equipped with a Dynon SkyView Touch primary flight display, together with Trig radio and Mode S Transponder, these give the cockpit a clean, modern and highly functional feel. For anyone considering purchasing a Bristell, TF offers an excellent combination of low hours, attractive presentation and modern avionics. For sale, a rare naturally aspirated 2015 G5 SR22 GTS FIKI – almost as new condition as its been cherished by its owner and lives in a lovely hangar at Exeter Airport. Some great options including yaw damper, EVS camera, active traffic, terrain awareness, Jeppesen chart view, safe taxi, Garmin Connect Satellite weather and phone & DME.

Free 3 day Embark transition training available with a CSIP. IR(R) & CB-IR available through our ATO to take full advantage of this incredible aircraft.

Description:
EI-GSM is a well-known and well-travelled 1998 Cessna 182S that has been used exactly as the type was intended. Regularly flown IFR across Europe, this aircraft has proven itself as a genuine touring machine rather than a hangar queen, and it shows in the way it operates and presents. The airframe currently stands at 4,469 hours total time, and the aircraft has been maintained on the Cessna Progressive Care AMP, with complete logbooks from new, reflecting consistent ownership and proper stewardship throughout its life.

Power comes from a Lycoming IO-540-AB1A5, producing 230hp, with just 299 hours since overhaul, paired with an upgraded three-blade McCauley propeller showing 559 hours since overhaul. With a useful load of 1,134 lbs, EI-GSM remains a practical four-seat aircraft with real bags-and-fuel capability.

The avionics suite is well thought out and proven, centred around a Garmin GTN 650 WAAS, dual Garmin G5s, and a KAP 140 two-axis autopilot, giving the aircraft strong IFR capability without unnecessary complexity. This is a cockpit that works, day in and day out.

Cosmetically, the aircraft retains its original OEM paint and interior, presented in a classic Cessna scheme that still looks right on the ramp and reflects careful, honest use. EI-GSM is currently operated out of Weston and is capable of operating comfortably from short grass or tarmac strips from around 400 metres, opening up a wide range of airfields across the UK and Europe. An experienced pilot pool and management support can be made available if required, giving a new owner the option to buy and sell hours to help offset the costs of ownership.

From a maintenance perspective, the aircraft’s ARC is valid through to 3rd September 2026, with the next scheduled Operation 3 maintenance check due at 4,492 hours. An immediate option for FAA US registration and airworthiness is also available, offering additional flexibility for overseas buyers or owners who prefer a US-registered aircraft. A properly used, properly maintained Cessna 182S with nothing to hide. Inspections are welcome, and the aircraft is available immediately.

Description:
This beautifully presented 1976 Cessna 182P Skylane combines a well-preserved 2,962-hour airframe with a freshly overhauled Continental O-470-S engine, a factory-new McCauley Black Mac propeller and an extensive recent firewall-forward refurbishment, creating one of the most compelling ownership opportunities currently available in the European 182 market.

Originally delivered in the United States as N86AD, the aircraft was ferried across the Atlantic into Germany in 1999 before joining the UK register as G-OJHC in 2007. It benefits from complete UK maintenance records, extensive ownership history and is supplied with a valid Annual Inspection and ARC until 21 January 2027.

The aircraft is equipped with the highly desirable Horton STOL conversion, including drooped wing tips, wing fences and flap gap seals, providing excellent short-field capability while retaining the renowned cross-country performance of the Skylane. Long Range fuel tanks provide 75 US gallons usable fuel, complemented by wheel fairings, strobe lighting and an excellent useful touring specification.

One of the strongest selling points is the recently completed firewall-forward investment. The Continental O-470-S has been professionally overhauled and has accumulated only 10 hours since overhaul. At the same time the aircraft received a factory-new McCauley 2A34C203/90DCA-8 Black Mac propeller, new Superior cylinders, refurbished engine baffles, new McFarlane engine controls, powder-coated engine mount and baffles, together with new Barry engine shock mounts. The new owner benefits from an aircraft that has effectively begun a new engine operating cycle.

The avionics suite provides an excellent IFR platform and includes:

Garmin GNS530 GPS/NAV/COM
Garmin GMA340 Audio Panel
King KCS55 HSI
Trig TT31 Mode S Transponder (ADS-B Out)
S-TEC System 50 Two-Axis Autopilot
King KN64 DME
Narco ADF841
Dual Altimeters
LC2 Chronometer
Four-place Intercom

Description: The Cardinal RG is basically the same airframe as the fixed-gear Cardinal. This may not have been a favor to the RG, since the fixed-gear model, introduced in 1968, had a number of well-publicized problems that took a couple of years to sort out. The RG, however, started and stayed with a fuel-injected 200-HP Lycoming IO-360 engine and had the leading-edge slots in the stabilator from the get-go.

Description:
A Prospective Co-Owner has already committed to acquiring a 50% interest in a factory-new Czech-registered TBM 980 and is seeking for a Second Co-Owner for the remaining 50% share in an exclusive two-owner ownership structure. 

The Prospective Co-Owner is prepared to proceed immediately upon identifying a suitable partner, with the objective of securing a production position and taking delivery during Q2/Q3 2027. 

The aircraft will be acquired through HLS Aircraft Sales s.r.o., Daher TBM's Authorised Sales  representative for the Czech Republic and Slovakia, and professionally managed by Jet O'Clock, providing a seamless ownership experience from factory order through delivery and ongoing operation.

Aircraft Acquisition:

The aircraft will be acquired through HLS Aircraft Sales s.r.o., Daher TBM's Authorised Sales Representative for the Czech Republic and Slovakia. This arrangement provides both Co-Owners with direct access to factory ordering support, aircraft configuration guidance, delivery coordination and local representation throughout the acquisition process.

Configure Your Own Aircraft:

The TBM 980 has not been configured or submitted for final specification approval yet. Both Co-Owners will have equal opportunity to participate in selecting the final specification, including exterior paint scheme, interior finishes, colour palette, equipment options, avionics selections, connectivity packages, mission-specific features and registration preferences (subject to availability). 

Rather than acquiring an aircraft configured by someone else, both Co-Owners will create the aircraft together from the factory-order stage.Professional Management Jet O'Clock will provide centralized operational oversight, maintenance coordination, scheduling management, regulatory administration, insurance coordination and ownership support, combining the flexibility of private ownership with the convenience of professional aircraft management.

Dedicated Pilot Arrangement:

Each Co-Owner may nominate a dedicated pilot of their choice, subject to insurance and operational approval requirements. The structure is suitable for both owner-pilots and non-pilot owners. 

Your Prospective Co-Owner: 

A Prague-based Prospective Co-Owner is seeking a like-minded partner to establish an exclusive two-owner TBM 980 ownership structure. The Prospective Co-Owner intends to use the aircraft exclusively for private, non-commercial purposes, primarily for personal and family travel within Central Europe. The objective is to establish a straightforward two-owner structure that provides both Co-Owners with excellent aircraft availability while significantly reducing acquisition and ownership costs.

Ownership Cost Structure:

A number of ownership and operating cost allocation models have already been discussed with the Prospective Co-Owner. While the guiding principle is that fixed ownership costs would typically be shared equally and variable operating costs allocated according to utilisation, no final structure has been imposed at this stage. 

Prospective Second Co-Owners are encouraged to share their own ideas, preferences and experience regarding cost allocation, scheduling and operational arrangements. The final framework will be developed collaboratively between both Co-Owners.

Equal Partnership Both Co-Owners will hold equal ownership interests and voting rights within the owning company. Major decisions concerning the aircraft, financing, disposition and operational policy will require mutual agreement.

Long-Term Stability Appropriate shareholder agreement provisions, including rights of first refusal and share transfer procedures, will be established to protect both Co-Owners and support a successful long-term partnership.

Delivery Timeline: The Prospective Co-Owner is ready to move forward immediately. Upon formation of the ownership entity and execution of the purchase agreement, the objective is to secure a production position with delivery targeted for Q2/Q3 2027.

Description:
AT Aviation is delighted to offer G-AMUF, an exceptionally well-presented and highly equipped De Havilland DHC-1 Chipmunk Mk21, direct from our Showroom. G-AMUF benefits from a zero-time Vintech Gipsy Major 10-2 engine installed in 2019, now with just 314 hours since zero time. The aircraft is fitted with Funke avionics installed in the front cockpit with remote controls in the rear, allowing operation from either cockpit. The engine can similarly be electrically started from either cockpit. G-AMUF retains its twin landing lights dating from its original Hamble training days and its comfortable touring seats fitted over the standard parachute-type seats. The aircraft has been fitted with 12 Gallon a side fuel tanks, giving it a longer range than most Chipmunks - (Circa 3 hours 20mins endurance in normal operation)

‍

G-AMUF (C1-0832), was ordered new directly from the De Havilland company in July 1952 by Air Service Training Ltd of Hamble as one of a batch of six aircraft. Delivered later in 1952, G-AMUF entered service training commercial airline pilots, principally for BOAC and BEA. It remained at Hamble and in 1960, when the organisation became The College of Air Training, continued training pilots there until 1971. During its long service at Hamble the aircraft received the successive AST and CAT colour schemes and accumulated an exceptional period of continuous operational service.

‍

In 1971 G-AMUF was declared surplus to requirements and was leased for two years to the East Midlands School of Flying at East Midlands Airport, Castle Donington. After which UF subsequently entered private ownership, where the owner had the aircraft repainted at Wycombe Air Park and based it at Denham. In 1976 G-AMUF entered a new period of private ownership, operating initially from Biggin Hill before moving to Redhill around 1977/78. Then in 1983, it was acquired by The Redhill Tailwheel Flying Club Ltd, which was established by two private individuals to operate the aircraft. From 1983 until 2019, they operated G-AMUF extensively throughout Europe and Scandinavia, with the aircraft touring as far afield as Malta and North Africa. In 1993 G-AMUF was stripped to bare metal and the wings were recovered before the aircraft was repainted in the scheme it carries today; the control surfaces have also recently been recovered.

‍

In 2019, after 36 years with the Redhill Tailwheel Flying Club, G-AMUF passed to its current owner, who commissioned the installation of the zero-time Vintech Gipsy Major 10-2. G-AMUF has remained airworthy throughout its life, apart from normal short maintenance periods, and represents a rare opportunity to acquire an exceptionally well-equipped and historically significant Chipmunk with an outstanding provenance, genuine long-range touring capability and a low-time engine.

Description:
The Citation 1SP is the single-pilot version of the original, turbo-fan-powered business jet in, what has come to be, the successful Citation family. The original Citation, after many changes and developments, penetrated the market in 1977 due to its ability to operate out of short airfields and at modest speeds, all at a low cost.

Initial changes to the design of the Citation 1 included thrust reversers, a longer wingspan (47.1 ft.) and higher operating weights, and were conducted in the last stages of development to ensure maximum competition with other similar jets of its time. Two Pratt & Whitney of Canada JT15D-1/A/B turbofan engines were chosen for the Citation 1. With each rated at 2,200 lbs. of thrust, they provide a considerable amount of power to fly the small jet.
